ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
22 General Precautions
Not everyone responds well or the same to medication.
The age, the habit of use, physical condition of the user or other circumstances may
vary the effects
of the drugs.

Always consult the doctor or pharmacist.
Use medications properly.
Never self-medicate.
Never mix drugs with alcohol.

question.es: El medioambiente, ¿se ve afectado por los accidentes de tráfico?

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

better condition of physical fitness,
have
better reflexes
and
skills
that are more

5 Narrow Sections

5

The following explains the order of preference in the absence of road signs, signals or authorised persons, and applies to priority when different types of vehicles approach a narrow road section and it is necessary for one of the vehicles to reverse back to allow the other vehicle to pass. Under these circumstance priority is given as follows:
1.Special vehicles and those travelling under special regulations that exceed the established masses and dimensions as per the regulated rules of vehicles (MAM).
2. Set of vehicles-except those within point 4 below.
3. Vehicles pulled by animals.
4. Cars that tow a trailer of up to 750 kilograms MAM and camping vehicles.
5.Public transport vehicles-designed to transport passengers.
6. Lorries, tractive units and good vans and goods vehicles.
7. Car and vehicles derived from cars.
8. Special vehicles that do not exceed the mass or dimension established within the regulating laws; heavy quadricycles and light quadricycles.
9. Three wheeled vehicles, motorcycles with sidecar and three wheeled mopeds.
10. Motorcycles, two wheeled mopeds and bicycles.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

It is also possible to avoid many of the risk factors that are connected with the vehicle, the road or the environment.

Road traffic collisions
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
With thought and knowledge it is possible to work out
where, when, how and why
collisions occur and therefore how to avoid them.
Certain circumstances related to the vehicle, the road and the environment but above all the driver, increase the likelihood of a road traffic collision or make the results of a collision much more serious. These circumstances are called

and avoiding or minimising them reduces the possibility of being involved in a collision.

explanation.text:
FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
13 Driver Distraction and Drowsiness Recognition (DDR)
The system assesses the driver’s level of attention in situations where he/she may lose concentration at the wheel, because of fatigue, sleepiness or other reasons.
The system monitors several aspects of the driver’s face, including how open his/her eyes are. It also analyses driving patterns and the driver’s reactions, combining them with driving speed data, the time and the use of indicators. If it detects that the driver is tired, it warns him/her by an acoustic or visual alert (displaying a coffee cup on the dashboard) or by making the steering wheel or seat vibrate, indicating the need for a break.

Aquaplaning
(also referred to occasionally as ‘hydroplaning’) is a frightening phenomenon whereby a wedge (or film) of water builds up between the tyres and the road surface. The
depth of water
on the road may be
excessive for the grooves
of the tyre
to suitably displace it
, which may also be heightened because of an inadequate depth of tyre tread.
This causes the vehicle to feel like it is “gliding or sliding on the water”. The result is complete
loss of normal control by the driver.
(Página 228 del manual 'Learning to drive')
Safe driving
5 Driving in rain
5.1.1 Aquaplaning
Aquaplaning is caused by the accumulation of water on the road and by irregularities in its surface. Therefore, when it rains, it is necessary to pay
special attention
to
potholes
and areas in which
puddles
may occur.
This effect is more likely to occur with inappropriate speed and very wide or badly worn tyres.
One of the best solutions to avoid aquaplaning is to
reduce the speed
in the first instance, so that the tyres can displace the water and the wheels can retain contact with the road surface.

explanation.text:

1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.

7 Driving on ice
When there is the presence of ice on the road, drivers should adopt the
same precaution as travelling on snow
. This means that, similar to snow, there is a risk of sliding and skidding. Always operate the hand controls and foot controls smoothly.
Turn the steering wheel, gently as it is particularly sensitive and the steering will feel very light when driving on ice. This is because there is reduced grip (adhesion) between the tyres and icy road surface. Smoothly and progressively, operate the clutch, accelerator and brake.
It is better to raise the foot slowly off the accelerator in a bid to lose speed. Try to avoid using the brakes, and always brake gently where necessary, so as not to lose control of the car.

loading
and

From

As
quickly as possible.
With
minimal noise
and
without causing annoyance.

explanation.text:
3 Use of lanes

Once a lane is selected, drivers should not advocate changing lanes unnecessarily but only when they need to change, in order to
turn, overtake, stop or park
etc.
The remaining vehicles (cycles, mopeds, vehicles for people of reduced mobility, etc.) must travel (within town) normally, only in the lane located to the right.
If the
lanes are not defined
, with road markings, then you must use the lane located to the
right
and only use a lane located to you left when you need to overtake or the traffic situation requires this.

question.es: Si ha cambiado de domicilio, ¿tiene obligación de comunicarlo a la Jefatura de Tráfico?
question.en: If you have changed your address, are you obliged to notify the Traffic Headquarters?

text.en: Yes, I must communicate my new address within 15 days.

explanation.text:
2 Driver documentation
2.7 Amendments to data and duplicates
The driving licence holder must notify the Provincial Traffic Headquarters, of any
amendments and changes required to the data
shown on the driving licence, as well as the address of the holder. This must be communicated within
fifteen days
(starting from when the change of circumstance(s) occur).
A
duplicate driving licence
will be issued, if the original licence becomes damaged, or lost, or due to changes to the data. If available, the original licence must be sent to the authorities upon application.
If as a consequence of a loss of a licence, a duplicate driving licence is issued, then should the original licence be subsequently found/recovered by the holder,
the original
must be returned to the issuing Provincial Traffic Headquarters.

question.es: Entre otros, ¿qué síntoma es indicio de fatiga?
question.en: Among others, which of these is a symptom of tiredness?

text.es: Disminución del tiempo de reacción.
text.en: A decrease in reaction time.

text.es: Movimientos constantes en el asiento.
text.en: Constant movement in the seat.

text.es: Sensación unas veces de frío y otras de calor.
text.en: Intermittent feelings of heat and cold.

explanation.text:
FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
10.2 Symptoms of fatigue
The
main symptoms
of fatigue are:
Difficulty concentrating on the road.
Blinking constantly, heaviness of the eyes and visual disturbance.
A reduction of hearing.
Feeling of having dead and heavy arms.
Continuous movement in the seat and changes of posture.
A feeling of pressure in the head.

question.es: ¿Qué puede favorecer la aparición de fatiga?
question.en: Which of these can contribute to tiredness?

text.es: La existencia de defectos en la dirección o suspensión del vehículo.
text.en: The presence of defects in the vehicle's steering or suspension.

text.es: Un buen diseño de los elementos interiores del vehículo.
text.en: Well-designed interior features of the vehicle.

text.es: Una vía en perfecto estado.
text.en: A road in perfect condition.

explanation.text:
FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
10.1 Circumstances that cause fatigue
10.1.2 Vehicle circumstances
Driving at night with
insufficient lighting
.
Driving with a
vehicle in a poor or noisy condition
(for example, having defects in the suspension or steering system).
Poor design
of the seat or other interior elements. An
ergonomic
seat helps to
prevent
fatigue.

text.en: Stopping.

6 Road marks

Yellow road markings indicating parking or stopping prohibition
Broken yellow longitudinal line – parking prohibited
: Indicates that parking is prohibited along the entire length of the marking on the side of the carriageway where it is located. May signify a temporary restriction, in which case this is indicated by a vertical sign at the start of the section. It may be placed either on the kerb or on the carriageway adjacent to it.

5.3.7 Signs indicating the end of a prohibition, restriction or obligation
R-500 End of prohibitions
It indicates the place where all previously signed prohibitions for vehicles in motion, lose effect.

question.es: Como norma general, en una autopista, ¿está permitido circular a 50 km/h?
question.en: As a general rule, on a motorway, can you drive at 50 km/h?

text.es: No, como mínimo hay que circular a 100 km/h.
text.en: No, you must drive at at least 100 km/h.

text.es: No, como mínimo hay que circular a 60 km/h.
text.en: No, you must drive at at least 60 km/h.

text.en: Yes, as this is the minimum speed allowed.

explanation.text:
5 Generic speed
5.3 Minimum generic speed
The generic minimum speed limits, both inside and outside populated areas, are:
On motorways and dual carriageways: 60 km/h for all motor vehicles.
On the remaining roads: the minimum speed is half of the maximum generic speed for each road.

question.es: Un conductor que tenga un resultado positivo en una prueba de detección de alcoholemia...

text.en: loses between 4 and 6 points on their driving licence.

explanation.text:
ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS
16 Alcohol limits
Driving with a BrAC greater than 0.50 milligrams per litre (more than 0.30 milligrams per litre for professional drivers and licence holders with less than two years experience) could result in the deduction of
6 points.
More than 0.25 and up to 0.50 milligrams per litre of breath (greater than 0.15 and up to 0.30 milligrams per litre for professional drivers and licence holders with less than two years experience) could result in the loss of
4 points
.
Driving
over the limit
of 1.2 grams per litre in the blood or 0.60 milligrams per litre in a breathalyser test is an
offence
punishable by the Criminal Code.

question.es: En esta vía con tres calzadas separadas, ¿por qué calzada debe circular?
question.en: On this road with three separate carriageways, which one should you drive in?

text.es: Solo por la calzada central.
text.en: Only in the central carriageway.

text.es: Por la calzada de la derecha y por la central cuando haya señales que así me lo permiten.
text.en: In the right carriageway and in the central one when there are signs that permit this.

text.es: Solo por la calzada de la derecha.
text.en: Only in the right carriageway.

explanation.text:
2 Use of the road
2.1 Roads with several carriageways
Where roads are divided into
two carriageways,
there is normally either a central reservation or barrier that provides a means to separate these carriageways. You
must drive
on the carriageway located on the right hand side.
It is not permitted to drive on the opposite carriageway in a contrary direction to that permitted unless this has been specifically set up and a diversion system is in operation. Neither is it permitted to use the central reservation area to carry out a ‘U’ turn.
(Página 161 del manual 'Learning to drive')
2 Use of the road
2.1 Roads with several carriageways
Where there are
three carriageways
, use is as follows
:
The central carriageway is normally used by traffic travelling in
opposing directions (two-way roadway) or in one direction
. The direction may be permanent or temporary and therefore it is necessary to consult the road signs and signals on this type of carriageway.
The
lateral
roads will normally be destined to
one way traffic
, without excluding the possibility of using the same or any of their lanes for traffic moving in the opposite direction, if duly signposted.

question.es: Si tiene el permiso de la clase B desde hace más de un año y ahora obtiene el de la clase A2, ¿está obligado a llevar una placa L en su motocicleta?
question.en: If you have had a class B licence for more than one year and now obtain the A2 licence, do you need to carry an L plate on your motorcycle?

text.es: No.
text.en: No.

text.es: Sí, en la parte delantera, durante un año.
text.en: Yes, on the front of the vehicle, for one year.

text.es: Sí durante un año, en la parte trasera.
text.en: Yes, for one year, on the rear of the vehicle.

explanation.text:
2 Driver documentation
2.5 Novice drivers
A person who obtains their
first driving licence
(permission to drive) will be considered a novice driver during the
first year
of holding their licence, as long as this period is not interrupted i.e. due to suspension etc. If a licence is reissued within this year, then the period is extended to take in to account the period of suspension.
(Página 22 del manual 'Learning to drive')
2 Driver documentation
2.5 New drivers
A novice driver must display a green rectangular plate, with a white letter ‘L’ on it, that corresponds to the prescribed dimensions legally required.
(Página 22 del manual 'Learning to drive')
2 Driver documentation
2.5 New drivers
This plate must be placed at the rear, to the
left
of the vehicle and remain
clearly visible
. However, it must not hinder visibility and obscure the vehicle identification plate or any signalling device. On motorcycles and three wheeled motor vehicles, it is acceptable to place it at the rear in a visible place, not necessarily to the left.

question.es: El conductor de un vehículo extiende el brazo horizontalmente con la palma de la mano hacia atrás, ¿qué indica?
question.en: The driver of a vehicle extends their arm horizontally with their palm facing backwards. What does this indicate?

The
reversing light advises and warns that the vehicle is, or is about to, reverse back
and that reverse gear has been selected. If an
arm signal
is used to convey this warning then
the driver must extend his arm horizontally and turn the palm of his hand backwards.

Indicates the proximity of an exit where you may carry out a U-turn but at a different level.

Broken down vehicles or vehicles involved in accidents
must be
towed
by vehicles
specially designed
for this purpose (assistance vehicles on public roads).

question.es: Cuando ha habido heridos en un accidente de circulación es fundamental...
question.en: When there are injured people following a road accident, it is fundamental...

text.es: darles algo de beber para reanimarlos.
text.en: to give them something to drink to bring them around.

text.es: sacarlos del vehículo para intentar reanimarlos.
text.en: to remove them from the vehicle to try to bring them around.

text.es: moverlos lo menos posible y llamar al 112.
text.en: to move them as little as possible and call 112.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
8 The rule - PAH
8.2 Advise: Request for help
To ask for help call the
emergency service number – (telephone) 112,
this will enable the appropriate emergency service(s) to be contacted. It is a
free number,
and can be accessed without operator coverage. This number is available not only in Spain but
across the European Union.
It is free, you can access it
even without operator coverage
, and it is available not only in Spain, but across the
European Union.
In the absence of a mobile phone an SOS phone can be used or if necessary, ask someone else to make the call.
The sign S-27, indicates the direction of the nearest SOS post or “closest help,” where it is possible to request assistance in the case of an accident.
The road sign may also indicate the distance to where this may be found.
(Página 259 del manual 'Learning to drive')
Road traffic collisions
8 The rule - PAH
8.3 Help: Assisting the injured
8.3.1 General rules
Don’t move the injured, unless it is essential for resuscitation or safety
.
Keep them still and
immobilise
the injured area
especially the head, neck and trunk of the body
and always avoid the casualty walking.

question.es: Invadir marcha atrás una intersección para incorporarse a la circulación, ¿está permitido?
question.en: Can you reverse into an intersection to then merge into the road?

text.es: No, porque está prohibido invadir un cruce de vías.
text.en: No, because it is forbidden to cross into an intersection.

text.es: Sí, si no recorre marcha atrás más de 15 metros.
text.en: Yes, if you do not reverse more than 15 metres.

text.es: Sí, si no obstaculiza la circulación a otros vehículos.
text.en: Yes, if you are not hindering the movement of other vehicles.

explanation.text:
Maneouvres
8 Reversing
As a general rule,
reversing backwards is prohibited.
However,
as an exception it is permissible
(but only when
travelling a minimum distance backwards – in reverse gear
), in the following two cases:
When reversing forms part of one of the following manoeuvre,
parking, stopping or joining the traffic flow.
In this instance the distance travelled in reverse gear must not be further than
15 metres
and you must not invade a junction.

question.es: Para ahorrar carburante, ¿dónde se debe poner el equipaje?
question.en: To save petrol, where should you put your luggage?

text.es: En el maletero.
text.en: In the boot.

text.es: En la baca.
text.en: On the roof rack.

text.es: En el maletero o en la baca, es igual.
text.en: In the boot or on the roof rack.

explanation.text:
Journeys and defensive and efficient driving
10 Factors affecting consumption
10.1 Air resistance
The majority of fuel consumed is used to overcome air (wind) resistance that acts against the advancing vehicle.
This means that anything that increases or changes the aerodynamics lines (the design) of a vehicle has a greater impact on consumption.
This is why
external accessories,
(roof racks, flaps and deflectors, etc.) increase the resistance of the vehicle and, therefore,
increase fuel consumption.
It is not advisable to leave
the roof rack on the vehicle
when it is empty and not being used.
It is preferable to carry the load in the boot, whenever possible and not on the roof rack.

question.es: ¿Qué indica esta flecha situada en el eje de la calzada?

Announces the approach of a continuous longitudinal marking indicating that driving on the left side is prohibited. Therefore, any overtaking manoeuvre must not be initiated—or must be completed as soon as possible if already underway.

question.es: La luz verde en forma de flecha del semáforo significa que los vehículos pueden pasar en...
question.en: The green light in an arrow shape on a traffic light means that vehicles can proceed...

4 Traffic lights
4.2 Traffic lights for vehicles

A
green arrow
that is illuminated on a
black background
means that the vehicles can
proceed in the direction indicated
.

question.es: Para un uso adecuado del alumbrado, ¿qué debe revisar?
question.en: To use your car lights properly, what should you check?

text.es: La regulación, el funcionamiento y el estado del sistema.
text.en: The controls, functioning and state of the system.

text.es: Nada, porque el alumbrado lo tienen que revisar en un taller.
text.en: Nothing, because the lights are checked by a mechanic.

text.es: Solo la regulación, pero con una cierta frecuencia.
text.en: Only the controls, but fairly frequently.

explanation.text:
ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES
2 Lighting systems
The functions of the lights on the vehicle are to
see and be seen.
The lighting system allows the driver, in low lighting conditions, to
illuminate
the roadway in order to view the road and
monitor the traffic
. In doing so the driver can see any
potential hazard
in time to react. For this reason, there is a need to frequently check the lighting system so as to ensure compliance with the lighting
regulations and operational use
. (Lights and bulbs should be checked to ensure they are working correctly. Make sure that the lights are not dirty or broken, etc.)
The
duration
of the
bulbs
(both conventional and halogen) depends on the
evaporation of the filament
. That’s why it
is recommended
, that if one needs replacing, the
other one should be changed
, too.

question.es: Advertir a otros usuarios de que se va a realizar una maniobra, ¿es obligatorio?
question.en: Is it mandatory to warn other users that you are going to carry out a manoeuvre?

text.es: Sí, siempre.
text.en: Yes, always.

text.es: No, pero es siempre muy aconsejable.
text.en: No, but it is always very advisable.

text.es: No, solo es obligatorio advertir a los conductores.
text.en: No, it is only mandatory to warn drivers.

explanation.text:
Maneouvres
2 Safety rules M.S.M.

After verifying that it is possible to undertake the manoeuvre
without danger, the
driver must warn other road users
of his intended manoeuvre.
If a driver doesn’t indicate his intention to undertake a manoeuvre, then other drivers and road users, will not be aware of a potential change of course, alteration of speed of the other vehicle.

question.es: El vehículo que sale de una vía no pavimentada, ¿a qué vehículos debe ceder el paso?
question.en: What vehicles does this vehicle exiting from an unpaved road need to give way to?

text.es: A todos los que circulen por la vía pavimentada.
text.en: All vehicles driving on the paved road.

text.es: Únicamente a los vehículos a motor que se aproximen por la derecha.
text.en: Only motorised vehicles approaching from the right.

text.es: Únicamente a los que se aproximen por la izquierda.
text.en: Only those approaching from the left.

explanation.text:
Priorities, level crossings and tunnels
2 Junctions
2.2 Priorities at junctions
2.2.1 Junctions without signals and signs
However there are exceptions to this rule:
Vehicles that travel on a solid road surface
(tarmac, concrete etc)
always have preference
over those that approach on a road not does not have a solid surface.

question.es: Los frenos, ¿son un dispositivo de seguridad activa?
question.en: Are brakes an active safety device?

text.es: No, son un sistema mecánico del vehículo.
text.en: No, they are a mechanical system in the vehicle.

text.es: Sí.
text.en: Yes.

text.es: No, son un elemento de seguridad pasiva.
text.en: No, they are a passive safety element.

explanation.text:
1 Influence of the vehicle in traffic collisions
1.2 Vehicle safety features
Active safety
is also called primary safety as it is any activity whose purpose is to
prevent
an accident, acting before it occurs and including
preventive measures
such as control of the tyres, brakes, etc.
Advanced driving assistance systems (ADAS) significantly improve the active safety of the vehicle.
Some security features
require active intervention
by the driver.
Lighting, tyres and brakes are
active safety systems
.

question.es: Al adelantar a una motocicleta de dos ruedas, ¿qué separación lateral de seguridad es obligatorio dejar?
question.en: When overtaking a two-wheel motorcycle, how much lateral distance must you leave between you?

Maneouvres
5.5 Overtaking
5.5.4 Performing the overtake
The driver should keep a
side-byside distance
of
at least 1.50 metres
when, outside of a populated area:
The driver of a
two-wheeled vehicle
is overtaking another vehicle.
The driver of
any vehicle is
overtaking
pedestrians
,
animals
,
animal transport vehicles
,
two-wheeled motor vehicles
,
vehicles stopped
on the road
or assistance vehicles
when
providing an assistance or rescue
service. Moreover, provided that the conditions are suitable for the manoeuvre, they move
partially or fully
into the
next
or
opposite
lane.

question.es: El vehículo lleva dos rectángulos amarillos con borde rojo. ¿Qué indican?
question.en: The vehicle has two yellow rectangles with a red border. What do they indicate?

text.en: It is a wide vehicle and measures more than 2 metres.

explanation.text:
Transporting people and loads
5 Plates and symbols on vehicles
5.2 Other distinctive plates, symbols, signs and stickers

This plate is placed at the rear of a vehicle to indicate that the vehicle or set of vehicles is longer than 12 metres in length. It is a yellow, reflective rectangular plate framed by a fluorescent red border.
Alternatively, smaller plates may be used and more conveniently located symmetrically on the vehicle.

question.es: La regla básica de actuación en caso de accidente es...
question.en: The golden rule in the event of an accident is to...

text.es: prevenir, atender y servir (PAS).
text.en: prevent, assist and help.

text.es: proteger, alertar, socorrer (PAS).
text.en: protect, alert and aid.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
8 The rule - PAH
Correct behaviour in the first 10 minutes directly after a collision is of vital importance as it:
Saves lives.
Avoids further collisions.
Reduces (up to 30%) or completely prevents secondary casualties.
Reduces damage to property.
Anyone who arrives at the site of an accident should apply the rule, which is represented by the abbreviation P.A.H. – protect, advise and help.

2 Driver documentation
2.2 The penalty point system
Regaining points
Anyone who has lost
some points
will recover the
twelve-point credit
if he or she
does not lose any more
in
two years.

maximum
of
four
points) by undertaking a recognised and established course of re-education and instruction of a
minimum
duration of
10 hours
. However, such a course may only be undertaken
once
, every
two years
(once a year for professional drivers).

question.es: En esta calle de un sentido no hay señales que prohíban estacionar. ¿En qué lado se puede estacionar?
question.en: There are no signs in this street that prohibit parking. On which side can you park?

text.es: En el lado derecho y en el izquierdo.
text.en: On both the right and left side.

text.es: En el lado derecho solamente.
text.en: On the right side only.

text.es: En el lado izquierdo solamente.
text.en: On the left side only.

explanation.text:
Maneouvres
10 Immobilisations – Stationary vehicles Stopping (waiting) and parking
10.2 Localities where this is permissible
In
urban routes
(within a built-uparea) and
in town highways
it is permissible to
stop or park on the roadway or the hard shoulder.
Where the roadway
is two-way
then the vehicle should be placed as close
as possible to the right hand side of the road
(in the direction that you are travelling in).
In a
one way road
it is permitted to park or stop
on either side of the roadway.
In all situations local municipal rules must be complied with.

question.es: Los conductores de bicicletas, ¿cuándo tienen prioridad de paso respecto a otros vehículos?
question.en: When do cyclists have right of way over other vehicles?

text.es: Cuando, circulando en grupo, el primer ciclista haya iniciado ya el cruce o haya entrado en una glorieta.
text.en: When, driving in a group, the cyclist at the front has already started manoeuvring on an intersection or has entered a roundabout.

text.es: Nunca.
text.en: Never.

text.es: Siempre.
text.en: Always.

explanation.text:
Priorities, level crossings and tunnels
3 Cyclists, pedestrians and animals
3.2 Cyclists
Bicycle riders have right of way with respect to other vehicles:
When driving on a cycle lane, a crossing for cyclists or a hard shoulder, all of them duly marked.
When the vehicle is
turning right or left
to enter another road, in the permitted cases, and there is a bicycle rider
near
the vehicle.
When cyclists travel in a group, and the first one has started to cross or has entered onto a roundabout, priority is afforded to the whole group –as if it were one long vehicle.
Note:
In all other cases the general rules, concerning right of way between vehicles will be applied.

question.es: Cuando en las inmediaciones de la calzada se encuentran niños con intención de cruzar, se debe...

3 Moderate speed
All drivers should travel at a
moderate speed
and, if necessary, even
stop
their vehicle when the circumstances require it. The following are
circumstances
that are likely to be encountered and where speed should be moderated to take into account the given situation:
When there are
pedestrians
on the part of the road that is being used or if rationally it could be foreseen, especially if it is
children,
the
elderly,
the
blind
or
disabled people.
There are
cyclists,

junction

of a
cycle way

question.es: Conducir con mal tiempo, ¿puede favorecer la fatiga?

explanation.text:
FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
10.1 Circumstances that cause fatigue
10.1.1 Road and environmental circumstances
Driving on a road with
heavy traffic
or with
many curves
.
Driving on a
poorly maintained road
.
Driving an
unfamiliar route
.
Driving with
adverse weather conditions
(like fog, rain, snow or excessive heat).
It is necessary to rest more often when driving in unfavourable conditions (for example, a lot of traffic, or in bad weather etc.)

2 Use of the road
2.2 Central refuges, isles, waiting area or guiding devices
When there are pedestrian refuges, central islands or channelizing islands in the road:
Normally vehicles must pass on the right hand side of these, in the direction of travel.
If these are located on a one-way road, they can be passed on either side.
If these are located within the part of a road assigned to traffic travelling in one direction only, vehicles can pass on either side.

5.3.4 Signs restricting access
R-200 No passing without stopping
Indicates the location of a mandatory stop.
Information is detailed on the sign and explains the reason for stopping, i.e. a customs post, police post, toll or other reason and purpose. Detention may be controlled by various measures, such as a mechanical barrier etc.

question.es: Ha quedado detenido en una intersección regulada por semáforos y obstaculiza la circulación, ¿qué debe hacer?

explanation.text:
Priorities, level crossings and tunnels
2 Junctions
2.3 Negotiating junctions
2.3.3 The Clearing stage
When a
vehicle has had to stop within in a junction
regulated by traffic lights and is
obstructing the flow and movement of traffic,
the driver must clear the cross section of the junction without waiting for the traffic ahead to move away. This therefore means that
the driver must change his course and take an alternative route.
Consideration must be given to other road users and the driver must ensure that he does not endanger the safety of others or block the advancement of other road users.

The belt (chest down)
The belt must pass on the
collar bone,
(clavicle) that is midway between the shoulder and neck, and must descend through the
centre of the chest
.
It should be applied correctly
and adjustments should be made either to the seat or height of the belt to ensure this. Wrongly adjusted or located it can cause
serious injury
in the event of an accident. If it is placed onto the shoulder, it could slide of in a collision and minimise the effectiveness of the seat belt.

result

question.es: La depresión es una grave enfermedad que se sufre cada vez con más frecuencia. Si se padece debemos saber que…
question.en: Depression is a serious illness that is on the rise. If you suffer from it, you should know that...

text.es: no es recomendable conducir de noche o por entornos monótonos o durante muchas horas.
text.en: driving at night, in monotonous environments or for many hours in a row is not recommendable.

text.es: si no nos medicamos no tiene efectos sobre la conducción.
text.en: if you are not taking medication, it does not affect your driving.

text.es: no debemos conducir hasta pasada al menos una hora de habernos medicado.
text.en: you should not drive until at least one hour after taking medication.

explanation.text:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.3 Depression
It is the
most common
form of mental suffering. The principal
symptoms
are: a sad mood, anxious or empty feeling, listlessness, lack of energy and feelings of hopelessness and pessimism. If suffering from depression, it is best to get
specialist assistance
as soon as possible.
(Página 48 del manual 'Learning to drive')
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.3 Depression
Depression affects the capabilities of the driver:
Increasing distractions.
The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.
Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant.
The driver
fails to detect
significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.
Increasing insecurity.
Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.
Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue.
It is advisable not to drive at night or in environments where road monotony may occur or for long periods of time.
Increasing irritability and anxiety.
A trivial event can provoke a disproportionate reaction by the driver.
In addition, there is usually the need for
psychotropic drugs,
which can directly affect the ability to drive.

unforeseen circumstances,
on the

when its

traffic lights

When dialling or sending a message.
To dial a phone number takes between 5 and 10 seconds and sending a long message takes a greater time during which control of the vehicle and attention is reduced or lost.
(Página 36 del manual 'Learning to drive')
DISTRACTIONS
8.1 Circumstances of collisions due to phone use
Research indicates that there are
four moments
especially dangerous when using a mobile phone whilst driving:
Whilst speaking.
Even with a hand free set, the first minute and a half of the conversation requires a high degree of focus and attention. After this time the driver fails to receive 40% of road signals and information and their average speed is reduced by 12% however they also take longer to react to a hazard or event.
When terminating a call.
The effect is worsened when the driver continues to think about the conversation. Normally, it takes some time for the driver’ concentration to return fully to driving and monitoring the traffic and environment.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

Safe driving
8 Driving in fog
Fog is very dangerous as, not only does it reduce visibility but the adhesion quality (grip) is also lowered, as the road surface becomes wet
.
Therefore, when driving in fog it is necessary to:
Use lights: the front dipped headlights or / and the front fog light (if fitted) together with the position lights and, in the case of thick fog, the rear fog light(s).
It is not recommended to use the main beam headlights as the fog reflects back the vehicles own lights (the water drops act like a mirror) and cases dazzle to the driver.
Keep the
cabin well ventilated
to avoid the windows misting up.
Adapt the speed
to the visibility and view of the road ahead.

Road traffic collisions
RISK GROUPS
5 Pedestrians
5.1 Children
Some of these limitations of children are:
Lower level of attention.
Those under the age of ten do not usually pay sufficient attention to the aspect of safety, so they can be easily distracted near roads.
They tend to confuse “ee”with “e seen.”
When they see a vehicle, they may automatically think that the driver has also seen them.
Unaware of traffic regulations.
Children are often not aware of relevant road signs or the proper behaviour required when near or travelling on the road.
Children are especially vulnerable, since their small and developing stature is likely to be adversely affected by an impact, particularly in the region of the head or other vital parts of the body.

explanation.text:
Priorities, level crossings and tunnels
5 Narrow Sections
5.2 Narrowing section without signed priority
5
.2.1 Order of preference in the absence of road signs
The following explains the order of preference in the absence of road signs, signals or authorised persons, and applies to priority when different types of vehicles approach a narrow road section and it is necessary for one of the vehicles to reverse back to allow the other vehicle to pass. Under these circumstance priority is given as follows:
1.Special vehicles and those travelling under special regulations that exceed the established masses and dimensions as per the regulated rules of vehicles (MAM).
2. Set of vehicles-except those within point 4 below.
3. Vehicles pulled by animals.
4. Cars that tow a trailer of up to 750 kilograms MAM and camping vehicles.
5.Public transport vehicles-designed to transport passengers.
6. Lorries, tractive units and good vans and goods vehicles.
7. Car and vehicles derived from cars.
8. Special vehicles that do not exceed the mass or dimension established within the regulating laws; heavy quadricycles and light quadricycles.
9. Three wheeled vehicles, motorcycles with sidecar and three wheeled mopeds.
10. Motorcycles, two wheeled mopeds and bicycles.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision
6.1 The young
6.1.1 The primary cause of juvenile mortality
Young drivers
generally have a number of advantages over the remainder of drivers, as generally they are in a
better condition of physical fitness,
have
better reflexes
and
skills
that are more
suited to driving.
However, these favourable conditions do not help if the driver is not aware of his
limitations,
including
lack of experience
or
the tendency to take more risks.
There are many young people who drive safely and therefore have no increased risk of being involved in a collision than other older drivers.
However, in Spain each year hundreds of young people die in road traffic collisions, which are the
leading cause of death in the 15 to 29 year age group.
Therefore the problem of road collisions is even more worrying for young people in this age group than for others outside it.
(Página 253 del manual 'Learning to drive')
Road traffic collisions
6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision
6.1 The young
6.1.1 The primary cause of juvenile mortality
The number of people killed in traffic collisions
rises rapidly from the age of 15 years
(coinciding with the entitlement to ride mopeds) and
again from the age of 18

is continuous until the age of 29 years,
at which time the
number of deaths starts to drop.

physical and mental aptitude
of the driver to be initially satisfied and thereafter maintained. It is therefore necessary to go to a

doctor
about the

ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS
17 Influence of drugs in road traffic collisions
The consumption of illegal drugs is related to many of the most serious accidents. A person driving under the influence of drugs puts all those around him/her at serious risk of accidents.
One of the effects of drugs is that risk perception
decreases
and some drugs can cause the driver to have an
incorrect
perception of
time and space.
The consumption of drugs will
never improve reaction time.
For people who take drugs and drive, the probability of having an accident is
greater.
It is forbidden to drive any vehicle with presence of drugs in the body. Substances
excluded
are those used under
medical prescription
and for
therapeutic purposes,
provided that the driver is
able to manage
the vehicle and drive with diligence, precaution and without distractions.

6 points.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

.

explanation.text:
Safe driving
5 Driving in rain
5.1 Adhesion - Grip
In order to maintain the best possible adherence (grip) between your vehicle and the road surface – you should:
Brake smoothly
and
early,
as the wheels can be blocked more easily.
Remember that if you drive through excessive water, there is the possibility that after passing through it, that the brakes (shoes or brake-linings) may be wet and momentarily ineffective. Check your brakes.
Step lightly
on the brakes so that they make contact with the drums or discs. This will enable the humidity to be eliminated –through the heat (drying effect) produced by friction
.

question.es: Si la temperatura en el interior del vehículo es muy alta, ¿puede influir en el tiempo de reacción del conductor?

text.es: Sí, disminuyéndolo.
text.en: Yes, by reducing it.

text.es: No, no influye.
text.en: No, it doesn’t have any effect.

text.es: Sí, aumentándolo.
text.en: Yes, by increasing it.

explanation.text:
Safe driving
12 The heat
High temperatures, present a potential risk that may compromise road safety. A temperature of
35 Â°C
inside the vehicle can constitute a danger similar to that of a blood alcohol level of 0,5 g/l.
Heat increases the driver’s reaction time. The driver is likely to make more mistakes, suffer from fatigue, become sleepy and more easily distracted.
Heat increases the risk of the driver becoming aggressive and hostile towards other drivers and road users.

question.es: Circula con un turismo que arrastra un remolque de menos de 750 kg de MMA en el que transporta mercancías. En cuanto a la distribución de la carga, ¿debe tomar precauciones especiales?
question.en: You are driving a passenger car towing a trailer with a gross vehicle weight (GVW) of less than 750 kg carrying goods. Do you have to take special precautions with regard to load distribution?

text.es: Sí, debe situarse en la parte trasera del remolque para bajar el centro de gravedad y asegurar la estabilidad del vehículo.
text.en: Yes, the load must be positioned at the rear of the trailer to lower the centre of gravity and ensure the stability of the vehicle.

text.es: No, salvo que supere la masa máxima autorizada del remolque.
text.en: No, unless it exceeds the maximum authorised weight of the trailer.

text.es: Sí, la carga debe estar bien distribuida e ir bien sujeta para evitar que se desplace y pueda llegar a desestabilizar al vehículo.
text.en: Yes, the load must be well distributed and securely fastened to prevent it from shifting and potentially destabilising the vehicle.

explanation.text:
Transporting people and loads
3 Transport of load
3.2 Placement of the load
When cargo is transported in, or on any type of vehicle, it must be carried in such a manner that it does not compromise the safety or stability of the vehicle.
The carriage of cargo will have a particular noticeable effect when the vehicle has only
two wheels.
The weight must be distributed so as not to adversely affect the
lateral balance.
If side boxes (panniers) are used on a motorbike etc., then the weight should be evenly distributed on both sides. Any load carried must be securely fastened.
(Página 216 del manual 'Learning to drive')
Transporting people and loads
3 Transport of load
3.2 Placement of the load
The conditioning and fastening of the load must be done to prevent:
That the load can move dangerously.
That it can fully or partially fall.
That it drags on the road.
The production of noise, dust or other disturbances that can be avoided.

It is a special lane that allows drivers to exit a roadway and adjust their speed to the road they are joining and without obstructing the traffic flow on the road they are exiting. Normally this is located to the right of the roadway but in certain instances it may also be found on the left.
In order to leave a motorway or a dual carriageway drivers must:
Pay particular attention to the road signing and locate in advance their exit road
.
Exit into the deceleration lane as soon as possible (where one is provided).
Reduce their speed within this lane, and without causing a hazard to other road users.

explanation.text:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.3 Depression
Depression affects the capabilities of the driver:
Increasing distractions.
The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.
Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant.
The driver
fails to detect
significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.
Increasing insecurity.
Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.
Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue.
It is advisable not to drive at night or in environments where road monotony may occur or for long periods of time.
Increasing irritability and anxiety.
A trivial event can provoke a disproportionate reaction by the driver.
In addition, there is usually the need for
psychotropic drugs,
which can directly affect the ability to drive.

and always watched over by a person. Said travel will be done on the alternative road with the least vehicle traffic.

Any one implicated, present or has knowledge of a traffic collision is obligated to:
Help
or
summons assistance,
to attend the victims, (if there are any).
Assist
to avoid further
danger or injuries
from occurring.
Help
re-establish,
when possible, the
flow and safety of other traffic.
Assist
and
relay
the facts of the situation and how the traffic incident occurred.
Communicate,
and inform (in all cases) your identity and that of anyone involved in the collision, when and if requested.
(Página 258 del manual 'Learning to drive')
Road traffic collisions

not applicable
to persons not involved in the accident or when their assistance is not necessary, such as when the
authorities
are already present.

explanation.text:

1 Priority and Right of Way
The driver of a vehicle that is obligated to
give way
or
concede the right of passage
to another road user:
Must show in advance his intention.
This means indicating his presence and movement by showing the
reduction of speed,
sufficient to allow others the right of passage or as necessary for the junction and road signalling.
The driver must not continue, or resume his intended course,
or complete his manoeuvre until he has conceded priority to the other users having the right of way. This entails not causing the other vehicles to change their speed or course by his actions or inaction.
Failing to comply with the right of passage by according precedence could result in the deduction of
4 points
.

question.es: En caso de reventón, ¿es correcto frenar bruscamente?

text.en: Yes

text.es: No.
text.en: No.

explanation.text:
ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES
4 Wheels
4.4 Behaviour in the event of a burst tyre (blow out)
In case of a tyre blow out (rapid deflation of the tyre) the following action is necessary:
Stay calm.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, with two hands, to correct any change of course that may occur.
Smoothly maintain the pressure of the foot on the accelerator, then, raise it slowly (do not abruptly move your foot off the accelerator).
Use brakes sparingly. Attempt to reduce speed primarily by engine braking.

3.5.1 Anti-lock braking system (ABS)
ABS, is a device that
prevents the wheels from locking under braking.
Sensors, installed in the wheels, determine whether the application of the ABS is required during the braking process. If the system detects that the wheels are on the verge of locking, the ABS

, so as to avoid the wheel(s) from locking. As the ABS prevents the wheels from locking, it allows the vehicle to continue to be

explanation.text:
12 Distances
12.5 Safety distance
The
safety distance
is the
minimum space
that a driver should leave between their vehicle and the vehicle ahead of them. This should be
sufficient
and enable them to stop,
without impacting and colliding with the vehicle ahead of them
, in the case of hard or unexpected braking by the preceding vehicle (the vehicle ahead of them). For safety it should always be greater than the stopping distance of the vehicle.
Not respecting
the safety distance from the vehicle in front of you is the
main cause
of
rear-end crashes
.
This distance should be increased when travelling at higher speeds or in reduced visibility, or where the road has low adhesion qualities and when the driver is unsure of the locality or lacks experience.
Not maintaining the safety distance with the vehicle driving ahead of you can cost
4 points.

6 Driving in snow
6.2 Visibility
When it is snowing or there is a covering of snow, there is the possibility that the driver will be dazzled (similar to when it is sunny) as the lights are reflected back off the snow. It is advisable to wear sunglasses and to use the sun visor to minimise the effect during the daylight hours. Road signs may become hidden – the line markings may not be visible and the vertical road signs may become covered in snow.

explanation.text:
1 Speed
Speed is measured by the
distance travelled
per
unit of time.
In the case of vehicles it is usually expressed in
kilometres per hour (km/h).
Speed is one of the
main factors
that affects safety. When travelling at
high speed
a vehicle covers a greater distance in the same time period, therefore, there is
less time and space
available to react adequately. The driver needs to
anticipate actions
a lot
earlier,
thus avoiding any problems that make it impossible to avoid an accident.
(Página 170 del manual 'Learning to drive')
12 Distances
12.1 The reaction distance
The
reaction distance
is the distance travelled by the vehicle from the time of seeing a hazard until he reacts to it.
It is dependant on the
speed
and the driver’s
reaction time,
which in turn depends, on many other factors, such as, the driver’s reflexes, their psycho-physical state (level of alertness, whether or not the driver is under the influence of alcohol etc.) Even the environment can affect the time it takes for a driver to react to any given circumstance (the passenger compartment temperature, noise, etc.)
A reaction time of
0.75 seconds
is considered to be
normal,
during which time the vehicle will travel a distance, determined by the
speed
at which the vehicle is travelling.

6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision
6.3 Drivers of two-wheeled vehicles
6.3.1 Bicycles
To prevent collisions involving cyclists,
the following is recommended:
Do not start or continue
an overtake
if there is a cyclists approaching in the opposite direction.
Exercise extreme caution in
bad weather or poor visibility,
because there is the increased likelihood of the rider falling or becoming unstable.
Avoid using the warning device
(horn) near cyclists. It should only be used when there is sufficient distance to avoid scaring or alarming them.
Be careful when you are
parking a vehicle or are near parked cars
or other obstacles, as cyclists are able to make sudden movements and change their course quickly.
Exercise caution in
housing estates and leisure areas,
especially in the
summer and school holidays.

19 The consequences of illnesses and drugs in traffic collisions
Sooner or later, everybody suffers from an
illness
that requires medication to treat it. Not all illnesses, or
medications
that are prescribed, present the potential risk that the driver will become involved in a road traffic collision due to the nature of the medicine or their state of health.
In Spain,
more than 75%
of people who are in treatment claim
not to have received any information
as to the
possible side effects
of the medication they are taking, despite the fact that the package contains information within it relating to its effects and
especially the effects when driving
.
This situation is unsatisfactory and extremely dangerous since it is estimated that the consumption of drugs is
responsible
, directly or indirectly,
for
10%
of traffic collisions, whereby the
basic skills
of the driver have been affected.

explanation.text:
ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS
16.1 Factors affecting alcohol limits
The time that has elapsed since the alcohol was consumed.
It is possible to detect alcohol
5 minutes
after consuming it. Over time this increases and a
maximum
is reached (called peak blood alcohol content) about an
hour later
. (Note: This may vary between 30 and 90 minutes) The level starts to fall below this maximum level
very slowly
with the effects lasting for    several hours and it will not completely disappear for a further period of time.
The type of drink and method of ingestion.
Alcohol is absorbed more quickly in
distilled beverages
(such as whiskey or gin) than through
fermented drinks
(such as beer or wine). In addition,
hot drinks or carbonated drinks
(fizzy ones such as tonics or other soft drinks) accelerate the absorption of alcohol.

8 Driving in fog
Fog is very dangerous as, not only does it reduce visibility but the adhesion quality (grip) is also lowered, as the road surface becomes wet

Use lights: the front dipped headlights or / and the front fog light (if fitted) together with the position lights and, in the case of thick fog, the rear fog light(s).

9 The negative effects of speed

When riding a motorcycle it is recommendable to wear
gloves
. If the rider falls or slips off typically the hands receive the force and impact as the rider automatically responds with the hands. Inevitably
grazes and wounds
, subject to the risk also of
serious infection
, will occur to the hands without gloves. The most suitable type are

ventilation

light in weight

ankles

leather,
with
small heels,
so as to hold well in the stirrups or rests.

using sandals, sports shoes or other unsuitable footwear that offer only minimal protection.

Safe driving
7 Driving on ice
When there is the presence of ice on the road, drivers should adopt the
same precaution as travelling on snow
. This means that, similar to snow, there is a risk of sliding and skidding. Always operate the hand controls and foot controls smoothly.
Turn the steering wheel, gently as it is particularly sensitive and the steering will feel very light when driving on ice. This is because there is reduced grip (adhesion) between the tyres and icy road surface. Smoothly and progressively, operate the clutch, accelerator and brake.
It is better to raise the foot slowly off the accelerator in a bid to lose speed. Try to avoid using the brakes, and always brake gently where necessary, so as not to lose control of the car.

ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS
16.1 Factors affecting alcohol limits
The time that has elapsed since the alcohol was consumed.
It is possible to detect alcohol
5 minutes
after consuming it. Over time this increases and a
maximum
is reached (called peak blood alcohol content) about an
hour later
. (Note: This may vary between 30 and 90 minutes) The level starts to fall below this maximum level
very slowly

hot drinks or carbonated drinks

20 seconds

dangerous situations

Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Studies show that traffic collisions are the
leading cause of death for men younger than 40 years
and the
fifth leading cause of death for men and women of all ages.
They are also the leading cause of traumatic spinal cord injury, the leading cause of work disability
and

People are often unaware about the real extent of the problem of traffic collisions.

Road traffic collisions
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
2.2 Factors involved in collisions
Generally, the factors that influence the occurrence of a traffic collision are varied, but always one or more of these factors are involved: the
vehicle, the road (& environment) and the driver.
Not all risk factors are equally important. Of every 100 collisions, only between
4 and 13 are due mainly to vehicle factors
(for example, a defective tyre or deficient brakes) and only
between 10 and 35 are due mainly to the road and related environment factors
(for example, when the roadway is wet and the vehicle loses control).
Most collisions,
between 70 and 90%, are due to the human factor
(for example, the driver becomes distracted, or speeds or is under the influence of alcohol etc).

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

question.es: Cuando llueve o hay viento, ¿por qué hay que tener más precaución con los ciclistas?

explanation.text:
Safe driving
10 Driving in cross winds (lateral winds)
Crosswinds can be very dangerous as the affect is to throw the vehicle off its intended course. It may cause an abrupt and sudden, unexpected movement or deviation. This is particularly
hazardous
for
two wheeled vehicles
or
vehicles pulling a trailer
. In cross winds, vehicles may even overturn or drive off the road.

question.es: ¿Qué peligro es el más frecuente al usar el teléfono móvil durante la conducción?
question.en: What is the most frequent danger when using a mobile phone when driving?

explanation.text:
DISTRACTIONS
8.1 Circumstances of collisions due to phone use
Using a mobile phone while driving can cause:
Frequent
change of direction and swerving
of the vehicle, with the possibility of lane invasion.
Problems in manoeuvring
due to holding the phone in the hand or on the shoulder.
Disorientation
and loss of perception of time, which can result in dangerous manoeuvres and excessive speed in order to regain lost time.
When talking on the phone is combined with other dangerous behaviour, like smoking or making notes,
the risk of a traffic collision multiplies
.

question.es: El freno de mano, ¿para qué sirve?
question.en: What is the hand brake used for?

text.es: Para frenar el vehículo cuando circulo cuesta abajo.
text.en: To brake the vehicle when we drive downhill.

text.es: Para dejar inmovilizado el vehículo cuando estaciono.

explanation.text:
CONTROLS AND ELEMENTS OF THE VEHICLE
2 Hand controls
2.2 Hand brake / parking brake
The parking brake is also referred to as the hand brake, since it is activated by use of the hand.
Keep the vehicle immobilised, with action generally taken on the
rear wheels.
It is normally operated by a
hand lever
located
between the front seats
or on the
dashboard
.
The hand brake must be applied after
parking
to ensure the vehicle remains
stationary
. It is applied by pulling the hand lever (handle) upwards.
(Página 85 del manual 'Learning to drive')
CONTROLS AND ELEMENTS OF THE VEHICLE
2 Hand controls
2.2 Hand brake / parking brake
It may also be used:
When stationary due to a long detention.
In incidents where the service brake and emergency brakes have failed.
When moving off on an incline (steep slope) to prevent the vehicle from rolling back.
In order to release the hand brake, pull the lever up slightly and press the button in to release the ratchet.
Then, keeping the button pressed in, move the (handle) lever down.

question.es: La cinta abdominal del cinturón de seguridad debe colocarse...
question.en: The abdominal seat belt must be placed...

text.en: over the hip bones or over the abdomen.

text.es: sobre el abdomen, únicamente.
text.en: only over the abdomen.

text.es: sobre los huesos de la cadera, siempre por debajo del abdomen.
text.en: over the hip bones, always under the abdomen.

explanation.text:
7 Seat belts
7.4 The correct fastening of seat belts
The belt (abdominal)
The abdominal part of the belt should be placed on the bones of the hip, always below the waist. If it is placed on the abdomen it could cause serious internal injuries in the event of a collision.
Once buckled, the belt should stretch slightly upwards and be tight to the body. Check that is not hooked or twisted at any point.

question.es: Como norma general, ¿está permitido adelantar en los pasos a nivel?

Maneouvres
5 Overtaking

It is also prohibited to overtake:
At
signposted
pedestrian crossings,
junctions with cycle lanes, level crossings
and nearby
.
As an exception, at
level crossings
or
nearby
, you can overtake
twowheeled vehicles
if, due to their small size,
they do not obscure vision to the side
. The manoeuvre must be duly signalled with the appropriate
sound and visual signals.
Similarly, at marked pedestrian crossings,
any vehicle can be overtaken if the manoeuvre takes place at
such a low speed
that the vehicle
can stop
in time if there is any risk
of an accident.

explanation.text:
6 Road marks

Broken longitudinal markings
A broken longitudinal marking is intended to
delineate lanes
to help guide the flow of traffic.
It means that
no driver
, whether of a
vehicle
or leading an
animal
, should
travel over it
except where
lane width
makes it
necessary
and
traffic safety
allows.
These markings
may be crossed
to carry out
certain permitted manoeuvres
, such as turning or changing lanes, always
respecting the priority
of the vehicle already travelling in the lane to be entered.

However, even if there is a pedestrian zone, provided that the necessary precautions are taken, the following may use the
hard shoulder

road

skateboards
,

question.es: Al aproximarse a un autobús en situación de parada, ¿qué precauciones se deben tomar?
question.en: When approaching a bus at a bus stop, what precautions should be taken?

3 Moderate speed
All drivers should travel at a
moderate speed
and, if necessary, even
stop
their vehicle when the circumstances require it. The following are
circumstances
that are likely to be encountered and where speed should be moderated to take into account the given situation:
In the proximity of a
bus,
either, nearing or stationary at a
bus stop,
especially a bus carrying out

Outside populated areas when
approaching
vehicles stopped
on

or
bicycles

the

question.es: Para disminuir la probabilidad de somnolencia debe evitar conducir...

text.es: durante las primeras horas de la mañana.

text.es: durante las horas de la madrugada.
text.en: during the night.

explanation.text:
FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
11.1 Causes of drowsiness
The most common factors that facilitate the onset of sleep and lead to drowsiness are:
The
time of day
. The
early hours of the morning
(especially between 3 and 5 a.m.)
and early afternoon
(roughly between 2 and 4 p.m.) are especially favourable for the onset of drowsiness, even if the driver has slept enough.

question.es: Cuando el autobús circula más rápido que el resto de los vehículos, ¿se considera adelantamiento?
question.en: When the bus drives faster than other vehicles, is this considered to be overtaking?

text.es: Sí.
text.en: Yes.

text.es: Sí, porque en vía urbana está permitido adelantar por la derecha.
text.en: Yes, because on an urban road overtaking from the right is permitted.

text.es: No.
text.en: No.

explanation.text:
Maneouvres
5 Overtaking
5.3 Manoeuvres that are not considered overtakes
5.3.2 Special lanes
It
is
not considered to be overtaking, when a vehicle travels faster in either an acceleration lane
– in order to enter a road; or on
a deceleration lane
- in order to exit a road and in doing so, passes vehicles. Additionally, this is also the case, in
a lane that is marked for a specific route and direction
or, a lane for
certain predetermined vehicles.
However it is considered to be an overtake, when a vehicle enters into an acceleration or deceleration lane purely in order to pass another vehicle or enters into special lane, whose function is to facilitate slower moving traffic.

question.es: Encender el intermitente, ¿da preferencia siempre para hacer maniobras?
question.en: Does turning on the indicator give you priority to carry out a manoeuvre?

text.es: No.
text.en: No.

text.es: Sí, porque he avisado.
text.en: Yes, because I have given warning.

text.es: Sí, pero debo hacer la maniobra rápidamente.
text.en: Yes, but I must carry out the manoeuvre quickly.

explanation.text:
Maneouvres
2 Safety rules M.S.M.
2.3 Carrying out a manoeuvre
After signalling the manoeuvre, and confirming that it is safe to undertake it – the next stage is to carry it out (execute the manoeuvre). This means adopting the correct position, the correct speed, and continually observing in order to ensure that no danger is caused to other road users.
It is necessary to bear in mind, that as a general rule, signals inform and warn of a manoeuvre only and indicate an intention to carry out a manoeuvre.
They do not grant right of way or priority to commence the manoeuvre or during its execution stage.
Each manoeuvre involves variations although the basic principles are the same, dependant upon the manoeuvre there are differences in the execution stage.

question.es: En esta vía, como norma general, ¿está permitido mantenerse en el carril de la izquierda?

text.es: Sí, si no entorpece la marcha de otros vehículos.
text.en: Yes, provided you do not obstruct other vehicles.

text.es: No, debe cambiarse al carril de la derecha.
text.en: No, you must change to the right hand lane.

text.es: Sí, porque la vía no está saturada.
text.en: Yes, because the road is not crowded.

On roads located outside built-upareas, where there are more than one lane for each direction of travel,
driver of automobiles
and
special vehicles with a MAM in excess of 3,500 kg
will normally drive in the lane located
furthest to the right.
When
traffic or road circumstances
thus advise, you can use the
rest of the lanes for your direction,
provided that it does
not obstruct
another vehicle following you.

question.es: Circula con su turismo por el arcén detrás del tractor para facilitar el adelantamiento del camión. ¿Es correcto?

Moreover, if a driver realises that they are going to be overtaken, they must
leave
as
much space
as possible, provided that there are no obstacles. As a general rule, they should
keep to the right-hand side of the lane
, without going into the hard shoulder.
However, if they are going to
turn left
or
park or stop
on that side, they should
keep to the left-hand side
, where possible, but without impeding vehicles travelling in the opposite direction.

question.es: Desde el punto de vista de la seguridad vial, el chasis y la carrocería tienen como función...
question.en: From the point of view of road safety, the chassis and the bodywork act to...

text.es: absorber la máxima cantidad de la energía producida en un accidente.
text.en: absorb as much of the energy that is produced in an accident as possible.

text.es: proteger a los peatones ante posibles atropellos.
text.en: protect pedestrians during a possible collision.

text.es: mejorar la aerodinámica favoreciendo una conducción económica.
text.en: improve the aerodynamics, thus resulting in economic driving.

explanation.text:
PASSIVE SAFETY ELEMENTS
6 The chassis and body
The chassis and body prevent or reduce injury to people travelling in the vehicle in the event of a traffic collision. The chassis and the body must
absorb as much energy as possible
to aid deceleration and
protect the occupants.
To do this, certain areas on impact suffer from a progressive strain (deformation structures / crumple zones) whilst the carrier compartment remains unchanged (interior cell security/safety).

question.es: ¿Para qué sirve el carril de aceleración?
question.en: What is the purpose of the acceleration lane?

text.es: Para alcanzar 120 km/h antes de incorporarse a la vía.
text.en: To reach 120 km/h before merging into the road.

text.es: Para incorporarse a la vía a una velocidad adecuada a las circunstancias de la circulación.
text.en: To merge into the road at a speed in accordance with the circumstances of the traffic.

text.es: Para incorporarse lentamente a la vía.
text.en: To merge slowly into the road.

explanation.text:
Maneouvres
3 Joining the traffic flow
3.2.3 Execution
If a vehicle joins the traffic stream, using an
acceleration lane,
then their
speed should be adapted, to a suitable speed that allows them to fit into the flow of traffic.
If there is a need to stop on the acceleration lane, because it is not possible to fit into the traffic stream, and the driver needs to give-way to the traffic on the road he wishes to join, then he should wait at the beginning of the acceleration lane.
This allows the vehicle to
build up the necessary speed, using all the length of the acceleration lane,
when a suitable opportunity becomes available.
Remember:
Sometimes, it is sensible to build up the speed on the acceleration lane in order than you can join the principle road
ahead
of the vehicles using it.

question.es: ¿Quién debe realizar las actuaciones de soporte vital básico a las víctimas de un accidente?

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
8 The rule - PAH
8.3 Help: Assisting the injured
First aid must be performed
quickly,
calmly and efficiently whilst maintaining a
calm and safe environment.
It is important to continue to monitor the casualties (there is a need to monitor their condition and how it develops).
It is so important to
know what to do and know what not to do. When in doubt it is best to refrain
from treating the injured so as not to make any injuries more severe. Give assistance in other ways, by giving
emotional support to casualties
(physical contact is very important) or by
reassuring them
until the arrival of professional help.

gripping the road surface,
it must guarantee good drainage away of the surface water from the tyre. The adhesion between the tyre and the road is reduced when the tyre is worn.
All tyres, (including retreads) must always
comply with the legal requirements.
This includes, not only the tyre tread and depth of pattern but also other abnormalities relating to the tyre-wall and tread, inflation pressure, bulges, exposed cords, cuts and other signs of irregular wear, and also the mixing of tyres etc. Basically the carcass (housing) must comply with all legal requirements.

M1, N1, O1 and O2
(See Unit 1, article 14) must, when used on the public roads (or places recognised as public thorough fares), have a
minimum depth of tread, of 1.6 mm,
in a continuous band in the main grooves of the contact surface.

for a motorcycle to have a
minimum depth of tyre tread;

explanation.text:

5 Overtaking
5.3 Manoeuvres that are not considered overtakes
5.3.2 Special lanes
It
is
not considered to be overtaking, when a vehicle travels faster in either an acceleration lane
– in order to enter a road; or on
a deceleration lane
- in order to exit a road and in doing so, passes vehicles. Additionally, this is also the case, in
a lane that is marked for a specific route and direction
or, a lane for
certain predetermined vehicles.
However it is considered to be an overtake, when a vehicle enters into an acceleration or deceleration lane purely in order to pass another vehicle or enters into special lane, whose function is to facilitate slower moving traffic.

Do not travel in parallel
(adjacent) to a twowheeled vehicle.
Maintain an
adequate and safe separation distance,
especially in town, where the two wheeled vehicle will travel easier and may advance quicker than anticipated.
Respect the rights of way
(priorities).
Exercise extreme caution in
bad weather or poor visibility;
it is more likely that the riders of two-wheeled vehicles will make sudden changes of movement and there is more likelihood that they will become unstable or fall off.
Technological advances in safety have also been made to two-wheeled vehicles, both to
reduce the risk
of accident as to
minimise injury
to occupants of these vehicles in the event of collisions. Motorcycles can also be equipped with stability systems, ABS and airbags.

explanation.text:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.3 Depression
Depression affects the capabilities of the driver:
Increasing distractions.
The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.
Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant.
The driver
fails to detect
significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.
Increasing insecurity.
Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.
Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue.
It is advisable not to drive at night or in environments where road monotony may occur or for long periods of time.
Increasing irritability and anxiety.
A trivial event can provoke a disproportionate reaction by the driver.
In addition, there is usually the need for
psychotropic drugs,
which can directly affect the ability to drive.

12.1 The reaction distance
The
reaction distance
is the distance travelled by the vehicle from the time of seeing a hazard until he reacts to it.
It is dependant on the
speed
and the driver’s
reaction time,
which in turn depends, on many other factors, such as, the driver’s reflexes, their psycho-physical state (level of alertness, whether or not the driver is under the influence of alcohol etc.) Even the environment can affect the time it takes for a driver to react to any given circumstance (the passenger compartment temperature, noise, etc.)
A reaction time of
0.75 seconds
is considered to be
normal,
during which time the vehicle will travel a distance, determined by the
speed
at which the vehicle is travelling.
