explanation.text:
ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES
4 Wheels
4.2 Tyres
4.2.3 The tread pattern
The tread pattern is the set of grooves in the tread of a tire. In addition to
gripping the road surface,
it must guarantee good drainage away of the surface water from the tyre. The adhesion between the tyre and the road is reduced when the tyre is worn.
All tyres, (including retreads) must always
comply with the legal requirements.
This includes, not only the tyre tread and depth of pattern but also other abnormalities relating to the tyre-wall and tread, inflation pressure, bulges, exposed cords, cuts and other signs of irregular wear, and also the mixing of tyres etc. Basically the carcass (housing) must comply with all legal requirements.
The tyres of the vehicles within categories
M1, N1, O1 and O2
(See Unit 1, article 14) must, when used on the public roads (or places recognised as public thorough fares), have a
minimum depth of tread, of 1.6 mm,
in a continuous band in the main grooves of the contact surface.
Note: There are other requirements relating to the depth of tread and pattern.

explanation.text:
8 Speed limits are a necessity
Speed limits are not capricious. There are numerous
factors
that determine the implementation of a certain speed limit being imposed, (for example; the designated speed, the acceptable degree of congestion, the demands of existing traffic, etc.) The aim of a set speed limit is to allow vehicles to travel with the maximum
guarantee of safety and fluidity.
One of the most important criteria is the
designated speed
of the road (the maximum safe speed that can be maintained on a section of road under favourable conditions). This means that a road is designated to be used at a certain generic or specific speed limit and traffic is not allowed to do a higher speed than that specified. To do
otherwise means that safety will be compromised.

Being a
novice driver
as this entails not having acquired all of the automated processes involved in driving, and therefore more concentration is required.
Adopting an
inappropriate driving posture
and position in the seat. This can result in pain, stiffness or muscular overload at the end of the journey.

14 Lane Departure Warning (LDW)

Mechanics and maintenance
9 The steering system
9.1 Improvements in steering systems
9.1.2 Progressive power steering
This type of steering complements the previous one, adapting the stiffness of the steering to the vehicle’s speed.
By means of a series of sensors, the system is able to register the driver’s behaviour on the steering wheel, the vehicle’s running speed and the engine speed. Based on these parameters, an electrical control unit instantly calculates the torque assist level required at any given time.
When the car is stopped or moves very slowly, the effort required to move the steering wheel is reduced to a minimum. However, at higher speeds, the steering will be slightly stiffer, which provides a more precise control of the vehicle.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

since it takes a long time to reach its temperature. If the
engine is petrol, start travelling immediately
after starting up. If it
diesel
it is appropriate to
wait a few seconds
for the engine  lubricating system to be properly greased.
When first travelling, keep to a
moderate speed
and wait
for the engine temperature to stabilise before making too many demands on the engine. Accelerating harshly or excessively with a cold engine will cause
premature wear and increase consumption.

question.es: Como norma general, ¿qué vehículo tendrá preferencia de paso en este estrechamiento cuando la prioridad no esté expresamente señalizada?
question.en: As a general rule, which vehicle will have priority on this road if right-of-way is not expressly indicated?

text.es: El vehículo que haya entrado primero al estrechamiento.
text.en: The vehicle that entered the narrow portion first.

text.es: El vehículo que tenga que dar marcha atrás mayor distancia.
text.en: The vehicle that has to reverse the furthest distance.

text.es: La motocicleta, porque tiene menos dificultad de maniobra.
text.en: The motorcycle, because it is easier to manoeuvre.

explanation.text:
Priorities, level crossings and tunnels
5 Narrow Sections
5.2 Narrowing section without signed priority
When there is a narrow stretch of road and there are
no signs or signals to determine priority,
the vehicle that has
entered into the restricted area first
will normal continue through having priority over vehicles coming from the opposite direction.
If there is however
doubt or conflict,
the vehicle that has the
greatest difficulty manoeuvring
will have preference.

question.es: Como norma general, una motocicleta, ¿puede circular por el arcén?
question.en: As a general rule, can a motorcycle travel along the hard shoulder?

text.es: Sí, pero solo si su cilindrada es igual o inferior a 125 c.c.
text.en: Yes, but only if the engine capacity is equal to or less than 125 cc.

text.es: Sí, pero no puede hacerlo en paralelo con otros vehículos.
text.en: Yes, but not alongside other vehicles.

text.es: No, debe circular por la calzada.
text.en: No, it must travel along the road.

explanation.text:
2 Use of the road
As a general rule, drivers of
automobiles
or
special vehicles
with a MAM
over
3,500 kg will drive
on the road
. It
is prohibited
for these vehicles to drive on the
hard shoulder.

question.es: Para transportar una mascota, salvo que exista en el vehículo un lugar destinado para su transporte, debe estar...
question.en: When transporting a pet, unless there is a specific place for its transport in the vehicle, it must be...

text.es: situada obligatoriamente en los asientos traseros y con el cinturón de seguridad del vehículo.
text.en: located on the rear seats and with a seatbelt.

text.es: sujeta de forma que no interfiera con el conductor para evitar que pueda perder el control del vehículo.
text.en: restrained so that it does not interfere with the driver, to prevent them from losing control of the vehicle.

text.es: controlada obligatoriamente por un pasajero.
text.en: held by a passenger.

explanation.text:
Transporting people and loads
1 Generally
It is necessary also for the driver, when transporting animals inside the vehicle, to ensure that they are suitably located and in a place where they will not interfere with the driver or compromise safety. This means placing them in a suitable cage and/or placing them in the rear (boot area) of the vehicle, separated from the driver and passenger compartment by a dog guard, bars or harness etc.
Never allow an animal to travel with its head out of the window, either keep the window closed or open the window slightly for ventilation purposes.

question.es: En una calzada con nieve, ¿el uso brusco e inadecuado de los frenos puede ser causa de derrape?
question.en: On a snowy road, can the sudden and inappropriate use of brakes cause skidding?

text.es: Sí, si se frena bruscamente los neumáticos pueden perder la adherencia sobre el pavimento.
text.en: Yes, in the event of sudden braking tyres can lose grip with the road.

text.es: No, si los neumáticos tienen la presión de inflado recomendada.
text.en: No, if the tyres are at the recommended inflation pressure.

text.es: No, si las ruedas están perfectamente alineadas y equilibradas.
text.en: No, if the wheels are perfectly aligned and balanced.

explanation.text:
Safe driving
6 Driving in snow
6.1 Adhesion (grip)
In order to improve the adhesion and road grip, and to prevent the risk of sliding and skidding, the following action is recommended:
When,
descending
(downhill) an incline, use a
lower gear than normal
and using the
engine as a brake
. Descend slowly.
Drive at a reduced speed
.
Increase the
safety distance
.
Use the
brakes smoothly
but don’ over brake.
Ensure that
tyres are in perfect condition
–correctly inflated and with sufficient tread.
Follow in the tracks of other vehicles (where the road surface has less snow).

question.es: Esta señal, ¿permite a un autobús adelantar a un camión que circula delante de él, si se dan las condiciones precisas para realizar la maniobra?

This sign prohibits lorries / trucks with a maximum authorized mass exceeding 3,500 kilograms from overtaking motor vehicles travelling on the carriageway, even when the manoeuvre does not require rossing into the lane reserved for oncoming traffic.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions

2.1 Driving safety
The driver’s response depends on their physical and mental condition, their training, their knowledge, as well as their skills and experience.
The driver must ensure that their vehicle is able to cope with the demands placed upon it. It must be kept in perfect meet comply with the law relating to its use. The driver must obey the signs and road traffic laws that relate to the vehicles movement and adapt their behaviour to the characteristics of the roadway (road signs road surface, etc.) weather conditions, the density or traffic flow, the vehicles load, and so on.

question.es: El conductor de una motocicleta que va a girar a la izquierda, ¿cómo señalizará la maniobra?
question.en: How does a motorcyclist turning left signal the manoeuvre?

text.es: Con el indicador de dirección izquierdo o con el brazo izquierdo doblado hacia arriba.
text.en: With the left indicator or with the left arm bent upwards.

text.es: Con el brazo izquierdo doblado hacia arriba.
text.en: With the left arm bent upwards.

text.es: Con el indicador de dirección izquierdo o con el brazo izquierdo extendido en posición horizontal y la palma de la mano hacia abajo.
text.en: With the left indicator or with the left arm extended horizontally and the palm of the hand facing downwards.

explanation.text:
Maneouvres
2 Safety rules M.S.M.
2.2 Signal: Advising and warning of the manoeuvre
All sideways movements, change of direction or ‘U’ turns must be warned of by the following means:
Using the directional indicator (lighting signal) that corresponds to the direction that the vehicle will be turning, or
With the arm horizontally extended and the palm of the hand indicating that the movement (change of course) is towards the side shown –i.e. left (for a left hand drive car –this is the correct method of indicating a movement to the left).
With the arm horizontally extended and bent upwards, and with the palm of the hand facing upwards and indicating that the movement (change of course) is to the opposite side –normally to the right. (Again this is normal practise for a left hand drive car / motor vehicle).

question.es: Cuando se ha comprobado que un herido respira normalmente, tras realizar la evaluación secundaria, ¿qué debe hacer hasta que llegue la ayuda sanitaria?

.

Road traffic collisions
10 Recognition of vital signs

(to attend to other victims),
place them in
the lateral
recovery position
, if possible maintanining the alignment of the vertebral column, this
prevents possible asphyxiation
should the casualty vomit or the tongue go to the back of the throat.

question.es: La marca vial es continua, ¿está permitido adelantar?

text.es: No, porque la marca vial lo prohíbe.

text.en: No, because the road does not have a hard shoulder.

explanation.text:
Maneouvres
5 Overtaking
5.1 Concept
Overtaking is the manoeuvre that consists of moving ahead by passing a vehicle or vehicles that travel in front of you at a slower speed.
Note: This also includes passing a vehicle in the same lane as you are travelling in and /or when it doesn’t involve a sideways movement.
(Página 186 del manual 'Learning to drive')
6 Road marks
6.2 Longitudinal road markings
Continuous longitudinal markings
A continuous longitudinal marking means that
no driver
, whether operating a
vehicle
or leading an
animal
, must:
Cross it.
Drive on it.
Drive to the left of the marking when it separates opposing directions of traffic (except in cases provided for in the traffic regulations).
A longitudinal marking formed by
two
continuous parallel lines has the same meaning as one formed by a single continuous line.
(Página 153 del manual 'Learning to drive')
Maneouvres
5 Overtaking
5.3 Manoeuvres that are not considered overtakes
5.3.4 Surpassing
If a vehicle that becomes immobilised for reasons
beyond the needs of traffic
is completely or partly occupying the lane of the direction of travel, you may
pass
it (without this operation defined as overtaking) after
assuring
that you can do so without danger, even when it is
prohibited to overtake
on the section of road in question and you must occupy part of the roadway reserved for traffic going the opposite direction.

Special vehicles and sets of special vehicles:
If they lack brake lights, or tow a trailer or are cultivators –a maximum speed of
25 km/h.
If they are capable of reaching a speed of 60 km/h on flat ground, and comply with the signalling regulations of vehicles: - a maximum speed of
70 km/h.
In all other cases, the maximum speed for the remaining special vehicles is

All these vehicles are
legally obligated
to show, to the rear of the vehicle, the sign
V-4

question.es: ¿Cómo debe sentarse el pasajero de una motocicleta?
question.en: How should a motorcycle passenger sit?

text.es: A horcajadas y con los pies apoyados en los reposapiés laterales.
text.en: Straddling the motorcycle, with their feet resting on the side footrests.

2 Transporting people

In addition to the driver and, where applicable, the occupant of the sidecar, a passenger may also travel on
mopeds
and
motorcycles,
when
thus stated
on the driving permit and meeting the following conditions:
The passenger is
older than 12 years.
That they use the appropriate seat
behind
the driver. In no case can they ever sit between the driver and the steering handlebars of the motorbike or moped.

and

text.en: No, they should complete it in a safe place off the road.

explanation.text:
3.3.4 ’Friendly declaration of an accident’- form
Road users whose vehicle has been involved in an accident must
not complete the accident report
on the
road
. They should complete it in a safe place
off the road
.

question.es: Los ocupantes menores de edad de estatura inferior a 135 cm, ¿en qué asientos de un turismo pueden viajar?
question.en: In which seats of a passenger car may minors who are under 135 cm tall travel?

7.2 Use
However, minors who are
135 centimetres tall or less
must use
officially approved child retention systems,
properly adapted to
their height and weight.
These retention systems must
always be installed
in accordance with the
manufacturer’s instructions,
as they indicate how they must be used and in which vehicle types to ensure safe travel.
(Página 76 del manual 'Learning to drive')
7 Seat belts
7.2 Use
Vehicles for up to nine occupants including driver
In this type of vehicle,
minors
who are
135 centimetres tall or less
must travel in the
back
seats and use the pertinent child
retention systems.

taller than 135 centimetres
may travel either in the
front
or
back
seats, with officially approved seatbelts that are
properly fastened.

question.es: Los límites de velocidad se establecen para garantizar...

text.es: la máxima seguridad, aunque disminuya la fluidez.
text.en: maximum safety, even if fluidity is reduced.

explanation.text:
8 Speed limits are a necessity
Speed limits are not capricious. There are numerous
factors
that determine the implementation of a certain speed limit being imposed, (for example; the designated speed, the acceptable degree of congestion, the demands of existing traffic, etc.) The aim of a set speed limit is to allow vehicles to travel with the maximum
guarantee of safety and fluidity.
One of the most important criteria is the
designated speed
of the road (the maximum safe speed that can be maintained on a section of road under favourable conditions). This means that a road is designated to be used at a certain generic or specific speed limit and traffic is not allowed to do a higher speed than that specified. To do
otherwise means that safety will be compromised.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
2.2 Factors involved in collisions
Generally, the factors that influence the occurrence of a traffic collision are varied, but always one or more of these factors are involved: the
vehicle, the road (& environment) and the driver.
Not all risk factors are equally important. Of every 100 collisions, only between
4 and 13 are due mainly to vehicle factors
(for example, a defective tyre or deficient brakes) and only
between 10 and 35 are due mainly to the road and related environment factors
(for example, when the roadway is wet and the vehicle loses control).
Most collisions,
between 70 and 90%, are due to the human factor
(for example, the driver becomes distracted, or speeds or is under the influence of alcohol etc).

It grants authorisation to drive motorcycles, with or without a sidecar, of a power not exceeding 35 kW and with a power/weight ratio not exceeding 0.2 kW/kg and not derived from a vehicle of more than double its power.
It grants authorisation to haul a trailer or semi-trailer whose MAM does not exceed 50 percent of the unladen mass of the motorcycle.
The minimum age that it can be obtained is 18.
Obtaining the class-A2 permit entails the concession of the class-A1 permit, therefore authorising holders to drive the vehicles permitted with this permit.
(Página 21 del manual 'Learning to drive')
2 Driver documentation
2.4 Classes of driving permits
2.4.4 A permit
It grants authorisation to drive:
All types of motorcycles, with or without sidecars.
Motor tricycles.
It grants authorisation to haul a trailer or semi-trailer whose MAM does not exceed 50 percent of the unladen mass of the motorcycle or motor tricycle.
The minimum age it can be obtained is 20, although until holders turn 21, they cannot drive motor tricycles with a power exceeding 15 kW.
It can only be issued to drivers who have already held a valid class-A2 license for at least two years.

To maintain an efficient engine it is fundamental that the fuel system is satisfactorily maintained. This means ensuring that:

It should be replaced when it is excessively dirty or in accordance with the manufacturers guidelines.

1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
13 Driver Distraction and Drowsiness Recognition (DDR)
The system assesses the driver’s level of attention in situations where he/she may lose concentration at the wheel, because of fatigue, sleepiness or other reasons.
The system monitors several aspects of the driver’s face, including how open his/her eyes are. It also analyses driving patterns and the driver’s reactions, combining them with driving speed data, the time and the use of indicators. If it detects that the driver is tired, it warns him/her by an acoustic or visual alert (displaying a coffee cup on the dashboard) or by making the steering wheel or seat vibrate, indicating the need for a break.

starting off

According to the revolution
Petrol

When it is possible for vehicles behind you to overtake, then in addition to leaving a sufficient separation distance so that in case of sudden braking by the vehicle ahead of you – you don’t crash into the back of it, you should additionally leave a gap to allow overtaking vehicles to overtake safely. 2.3 Carrying out a manoeuvre
After signalling the manoeuvre, and confirming that it is safe to undertake it – the next stage is to carry it out (execute the manoeuvre). This means adopting the correct position, the correct speed, and continually observing in order to ensure that no danger is caused to other road users.
It is necessary to bear in mind, that as a general rule, signals inform and warn of a manoeuvre only and indicate an intention to carry out a manoeuvre.

Each manoeuvre involves variations although the basic principles are the same, dependant upon the manoeuvre there are differences in the execution stage.

Use brakes sparingly. Attempt to reduce speed primarily by engine braking.

ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.1 Respiratory allergies
Tips for drivers with allergies:
Not drive with the windows open.
The air will contain large quantities of pollen, so it will increase the allergic reaction.
Do not put the air conditioning on strongly.
The direct jets of air will cause an allergic reaction.
Keep the ventilation ducts clean.
Clean the inside of the vehicle frequently, especially if animals are transported, and if possible fit special HEPA filters (high efficiency particulate air).
The holding capacity of the cabin air filter is limited. It is recommended to check it periodically, especially at the beginning of spring, replacing it if necessary.

explanation.text:
12 Distances
12.5 Safety distance
The
safety distance
is the
minimum space
that a driver should leave between their vehicle and the vehicle ahead of them. This should be
sufficient
and enable them to stop,
without impacting and colliding with the vehicle ahead of them
, in the case of hard or unexpected braking by the preceding vehicle (the vehicle ahead of them). For safety it should always be greater than the stopping distance of the vehicle.
Not respecting
the safety distance from the vehicle in front of you is the
main cause
of
rear-end crashes
.
This distance should be increased when travelling at higher speeds or in reduced visibility, or where the road has low adhesion qualities and when the driver is unsure of the locality or lacks experience.
Not maintaining the safety distance with the vehicle driving ahead of you can cost
4 points.
(Página 180 del manual 'Learning to drive')
12 Distances
12.5 Safety distance
Any driver of a vehicle driving behind another must leave space that allows them to stop without colliding in the event of sudden braking, taking into account, in particular, speed, grip and braking conditions. However, a group of cyclists does not need to keep this distance, paying close attention to avoid collisions.
When it is possible for vehicles behind you to overtake, then in addition to leaving a sufficient separation distance so that in case of sudden braking by the vehicle ahead of you – you don’t crash into the back of it, you should additionally leave a gap to allow overtaking vehicles to overtake safely. (Note: that his rule is not applicable to a group of cyclists travelling together.)
Vehicles with a
MAM greater than 3500 kgs,
vehicles and combinations / sets of
vehicles over 10m long,
must keep a
minimum safety distance of 50 m.
(Página 180 del manual 'Learning to drive')

In a built-up-area
(within town and cities etc.)
.

Where there is
more than 1 lane
for the direction travelled

intense traffic
does not permit overtaking.

12.5 Safety distance
Any driver of a vehicle driving behind another must leave space that allows them to stop without colliding in the event of sudden braking, taking into account, in particular, speed, grip and braking conditions. When it is possible for vehicles behind you to overtake, then in addition to leaving a sufficient separation distance so that in case of sudden braking by the vehicle ahead of you – you don’t crash into the back of it, you should additionally leave a gap to allow overtaking vehicles to overtake safely. (Note: that his rule is not applicable to a group of cyclists travelling together.)

MAM greater than 3500 kgs,

Road traffic collisions
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
2.2 Factors involved in collisions
Generally, the factors that influence the occurrence of a traffic collision are varied, but always one or more of these factors are involved: the
vehicle, the road (& environment) and the driver.
Not all risk factors are equally important. Of every 100 collisions, only between
4 and 13 are due mainly to vehicle factors
(for example, a defective tyre or deficient brakes) and only
between 10 and 35 are due mainly to the road and related environment factors
(for example, when the roadway is wet and the vehicle loses control).
Most collisions,
between 70 and 90%, are due to the human factor
(for example, the driver becomes distracted, or speeds or is under the influence of alcohol etc).

question.es: ¿Cómo se denominan los costes de pérdida de vidas, de capacidad productiva y el sufrimiento físico y psicológico que tienen lugar como consecuencia de un accidente de tráfico?

text.es: Costes sanitarios.
text.en: Medical costs.

text.es: Costes humanos.
text.en: Human costs.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.

16.2 Effects of Alcohol
Changes that alcohol produces in the driver’s physical capabilities:
It alters the ability to undertake movements with
precision
and
coordination.
It makes the driver’ coordination
more difficult
, so that he cannot accurately assess his surroundings and the
movement
of other road users.
Impact of alcohol on the driver’ decision-making abilities:
It increases the reaction time
during which the vehicle will travel further before the driver responds.
It increases
the likelihood that the driver will make
wrong decisions.
It leads to the driver implementing
decisions ineffectively.
(Página 43 del manual 'Learning to drive')
12 Distances
12.1 The reaction distance
The
reaction distance
is the distance travelled by the vehicle from the time of seeing a hazard until he reacts to it.
It is dependant on the
speed
and the driver’s
reaction time,
which in turn depends, on many other factors, such as, the driver’s reflexes, their psycho-physical state (level of alertness, whether or not the driver is under the influence of alcohol etc.) Even the environment can affect the time it takes for a driver to react to any given circumstance (the passenger compartment temperature, noise, etc.)
A reaction time of
0.75 seconds
is considered to be
normal,
during which time the vehicle will travel a distance, determined by the
speed
at which the vehicle is travelling.

novice driver

inappropriate driving posture

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
2.3 The key: Reducing the risk
It is also possible to avoid many of the risk factors that are connected with the vehicle, the road or the environment.
In many collisions, the driver claims that the vehicle or road was an associated or main factor but the simple truth is that the driver could have behaved in a different way that would have avoided a collision. For example, if the driver had realised that the tyres were defective (by maintenance and inspection) they could have avoided the puncture (blow out) or if they had adopted an adequate speed and a safe distance when driving in the rain or snow, they could have avoided running into the vehicle ahead of them.
Proper maintenance and responsible driving reduces the chances that a “vehicle factor” or a “road factor” will be a cause of a collision.

8 Speed limits are a necessity
Speed limits are not capricious. There are numerous
factors
that determine the implementation of a certain speed limit being imposed, (for example; the designated speed, the acceptable degree of congestion, the demands of existing traffic, etc.) The aim of a set speed limit is to allow vehicles to travel with the maximum
guarantee of safety and fluidity.
One of the most important criteria is the
designated speed
of the road (the maximum safe speed that can be maintained on a section of road under favourable conditions). This means that a road is designated to be used at a certain generic or specific speed limit and traffic is not allowed to do a higher speed than that specified. To do
otherwise means that safety will be compromised.

explanation.text:
7 Seat belts
7.1 Purpose and effectiveness
The purpose of a seat belt is to
retain and protect
the
driver and occupants
in the event of sudden stopping, collision or the vehicle rolling over. The seat belt
prevents
the occupants of a vehicle from being
catapulted out
of it and
absorbs
part of the energy of an impact.
During a frontal collision against an indeformable object, a vehicle stops in a tenth of a second, but due to inertia, the occupants will continue moving
at the same speed
as the
vehicle
was travelling at. Therefore, there is the likelihood of colliding with the steering wheel or the windshield, which will result in
serious injuries
being sustained.
To avoid this, the seat belt slows the movement of the body by
stretching out
, as if is made of an elastic material, by an extensible action.
(Página 75 del manual 'Learning to drive')
7 Seat belts
7.6 Misconceptions of safety belts
“It is dangerous to use a seat belt during pregnancy”
The use of seat belts is compulsory for pregnant women, as they have proved that if you are not wearing it, the foetus can suffer major damage in the event of an accident.
The abdominal belt must go as low as possible on the hips, to wear it higher could potentially harm the baby. There are devices on the market that adequately prevent the belt from going up onto the abdomen.
“The belt is only necessary for front seat passengers. In the rear seats it isn’ necessary”
If passengers in the rear seats fail to wear a seat belt there is the probability that, in the event of a frontal collision, they will be fired forwards towards the occupants in the front seats and serious injury will be caused.
The likelihood for an occupant in the rear seats to cause the death of another passenger in the front seats due to the fact that they are launched forward is up to 8 times greater than if the seat belt is worn.

question.es: Los accidentes de tráfico, ¿causan costes administrativos?
question.en: Do traffic accidents cause administrative costs?

text.es: No, solo materiales.

text.es: Sí, entre otros de policía y bomberos.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

Road traffic collisions
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
The reality is that
most road traffic collision deaths could have been avoided.
The misconception is the belief that these are accidents, they aren’t – most of the events are
predictable and therefore preventable.
For this reason the term ‘accident’ has been replaced by the word ‘collision’ because invariably someone is responsible.
(Página 249 del manual 'Learning to drive')
Road traffic collisions
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
With thought and knowledge it is possible to work out
where, when, how and why
collisions occur and therefore how to avoid them.
Certain circumstances related to the vehicle, the road and the environment but above all the driver, increase the likelihood of a road traffic collision or make the results of a collision much more serious. These circumstances are called
“risk factors”
and avoiding or minimising them reduces the possibility of being involved in a collision.
Some of these risk factors are fatigue, alcohol, excessive speed, ice or driving with a poorly maintained vehicle, particularly worn tyres.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.3 Depression
Depression affects the capabilities of the driver:
Increasing distractions.
The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.
Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant.
The driver
fails to detect
significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.
Increasing insecurity.
Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.
Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue.
It is advisable not to drive at night or in environments where road monotony may occur or for long periods of time.
Increasing irritability and anxiety.
A trivial event can provoke a disproportionate reaction by the driver.
In addition, there is usually the need for
psychotropic drugs,
which can directly affect the ability to drive.

DEFENSIVE DRIVING
4 Observation

4.3.2 Blind Spot Monitoring (BSM)
The system warns the driver of the presence of another vehicle in the next lane in the blind spot by displaying a light in the rear-view mirror on that side. The most effective systems only give this warning when the driver uses the indicators to change lane.
There are other more advanced systems that can act on the steering and brakes; when the driver tries to switch to a lane occupied by another vehicle, they apply resistance to the steering wheel and slightly reduce the vehicle’s speed.

12 Distances
12.3 The stopping distance
The
overall stopping distance
is the
distance the vehicle takes to come to a complete stop
from the point at which the
driver first sees the hazard to the point the vehicle comes to a final stop.
In other words it is the result of adding the reaction distance and the braking distance together.
(Página 179 del manual 'Learning to drive')
12 Distances
12.3 The stopping distance
The stopping distances will always increase
if
the reaction distance/time or the braking distance increases.
As a result the stopping distance of a vehicle ultimately depends upon its speed. However
other factors can additionally have an influence on this.
It can thus be seen that the
stopping distance
of the vehicle will depend on its
speed
and the condition of the
driver
, the
road surface
and the
vehicle
itself.

12 Distances

The braking distance is the
distance the vehicle travels
from the point at which the driver first
applies the brakes,

complete stop.
This distance can vary depending on:
The
speed
of the vehicle at the point the brakes are applied.
The
mass
of the
vehicle
and its
load.
The
technical condition
of the vehicle (brakes, tyres, shock absorbers, etc.)
The

road surface

The
driver
(psychophysical status –mental and physical state, experience, etc.)
An
increase
in
speed

ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS
17 Influence of drugs in road traffic collisions
The consumption of illegal drugs is related to many of the most serious accidents. A person driving under the influence of drugs puts all those around him/her at serious risk of accidents.
One of the effects of drugs is that risk perception
decreases
and some drugs can cause the driver to have an
incorrect
perception of
time and space.
The consumption of drugs will
never improve reaction time.
For people who take drugs and drive, the probability of having an accident is
greater.
It is forbidden to drive any vehicle with presence of drugs in the body. Substances
excluded
are those used under
medical prescription
and for
therapeutic purposes,
provided that the driver is
able to manage
the vehicle and drive with diligence, precaution and without distractions.
Driving with drugs present in the body may result in the loss of
6 points.

2 Driver documentation

2.4.1 A1 permit
It grants authorisation to drive:
Vehicles for people with reduced mobility.

Motor tricycles with a power not exceeding 15 kW.
Obtaining the class-A1 permit entails the concession of the AM-class permit, therefore authorising the holder to drive the same vehicles (two or
three-wheeled mopeds and light quadricycles).
It grants authorisation to haul a trailer or semi-trailer whose MAM does not exceed 50 percent of the unladen mass of the motorcycle or motor tricycle.

explanation.text:
Safe driving
8 Driving in fog
Fog is very dangerous as, not only does it reduce visibility but the adhesion quality (grip) is also lowered, as the road surface becomes wet
.
Therefore, when driving in fog it is necessary to:
Use lights: the front dipped headlights or / and the front fog light (if fitted) together with the position lights and, in the case of thick fog, the rear fog light(s).
It is not recommended to use the main beam headlights as the fog reflects back the vehicles own lights (the water drops act like a mirror) and cases dazzle to the driver.
Keep the
cabin well ventilated
to avoid the windows misting up.
Adapt the speed
to the visibility and view of the road ahead.
(Página 232 del manual 'Learning to drive')
Safe driving
8 Driving in fog
Therefore, when driving in fog it is necessary to:
Increase the safety distance.
Pay extra attention
to the
road markings
and
traffic guidance signs.
Avoid overtaking
and overtake only when there is sufficient visibility.
Be very careful at
and on the approach to junctions
.

question.es: Como norma general, ¿cuándo es mayor el efecto del alcohol?
question.en: As a general rule, when is the effect of alcohol greater?

text.es: Tres horas después de tomarlo.
text.en: Three hours after drinking.

text.es: Entre 30 y 90 minutos después de haber ingerido el alcohol.
text.en: Between 30 and 90 minutes after you have drunk the alcohol.

text.es: Inmediatamente después de tomarlo.
text.en: Immediately after drinking.

explanation.text:
ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS
16.1 Factors affecting alcohol limits
The time that has elapsed since the alcohol was consumed.
It is possible to detect alcohol
5 minutes
after consuming it. Over time this increases and a
maximum
is reached (called peak blood alcohol content) about an
hour later
. (Note: This may vary between 30 and 90 minutes) The level starts to fall below this maximum level
very slowly
with the effects lasting for    several hours and it will not completely disappear for a further period of time.
The type of drink and method of ingestion.
Alcohol is absorbed more quickly in
distilled beverages
(such as whiskey or gin) than through
fermented drinks
(such as beer or wine). In addition,
hot drinks or carbonated drinks
(fizzy ones such as tonics or other soft drinks) accelerate the absorption of alcohol.

question.es: Los accidentes de tráfico constituyen una de las principales causas de mortalidad que afectan sobre todo a...

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision
6.1 The young
6.1.1 The primary cause of juvenile mortality
Young drivers
generally have a number of advantages over the remainder of drivers, as generally they are in a
better condition of physical fitness,
have
better reflexes
and
skills
that are more
suited to driving.
However, these favourable conditions do not help if the driver is not aware of his
limitations,
including
lack of experience
or
the tendency to take more risks.
There are many young people who drive safely and therefore have no increased risk of being involved in a collision than other older drivers.
However, in Spain each year hundreds of young people die in road traffic collisions, which are the
leading cause of death in the 15 to 29 year age group.
Therefore the problem of road collisions is even more worrying for young people in this age group than for others outside it.

explanation.text:
ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS
16.2 Effects of Alcohol
Changes that alcohol produces in the driver’s physical capabilities:
It alters the ability to undertake movements with
precision
and
coordination.
It makes the driver’ coordination
more difficult
, so that he cannot accurately assess his surroundings and the
movement
of other road users.
Impact of alcohol on the driver’ decision-making abilities:
It increases the reaction time
during which the vehicle will travel further before the driver responds.
It increases
the likelihood that the driver will make
wrong decisions.
It leads to the driver implementing
decisions ineffectively.

explanation.text:
ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES
4 Wheels
4.2 Tyres
4.2.3 The tread pattern
The tread pattern is the set of grooves in the tread of a tire. In addition to
gripping the road surface,
it must guarantee good drainage away of the surface water from the tyre. The adhesion between the tyre and the road is reduced when the tyre is worn.
All tyres, (including retreads) must always
comply with the legal requirements.
This includes, not only the tyre tread and depth of pattern but also other abnormalities relating to the tyre-wall and tread, inflation pressure, bulges, exposed cords, cuts and other signs of irregular wear, and also the mixing of tyres etc. Basically the carcass (housing) must comply with all legal requirements.
The tyres of the vehicles within categories
M1, N1, O1 and O2
(See Unit 1, article 14) must, when used on the public roads (or places recognised as public thorough fares), have a
minimum depth of tread, of 1.6 mm,
in a continuous band in the main grooves of the contact surface.
Note: There are other requirements relating to the depth of tread and pattern.
(Página 70 del manual 'Learning to drive')
ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES
4 Wheels
4.2 Tyres
4.2.3 The tread pattern
Regrooving
(which consists of recutting part of the tread pattern into the tyre) are
not allowed,
except on tyres for vehicles over 3.5 tons of MAM and that clearly display the word “Regroovable” or the symbol U.
Tyres used on cars and trailers, which comply with legal requirements, must also have ‘tyre wear indicators’ (or TWI). The purpose of the tyre wear indicators is to indicate that the main grooves (within the central band) have reached the minimum depth of tread permitted.
Drivers must maintain their tyre and ensure that the tread reaches the required legal standard. It is advisable to replace them when the depth of the pattern is below 2 mm.

text.es: Ayuda a mantener la velocidad de circulación en el valor constante que elija el conductor, sin necesidad de pisar el acelerador.
text.en: It helps to maintain the driving speed at a constant speed chosen by the driver, without needing to step on the accelerator.

text.es: Muestra el límite de velocidad en la vía por la que se circula y ayuda al conductor a mantener una velocidad apropiada en ese entorno proporcionándole una información adecuada.
text.en: It displays the speed limit on the road on which it is being driven and helps the driver to maintain an appropriate speed in that environment by providing appropriate information.

text.es: Se encarga de no rebasar una velocidad de circulación, velocidad limitada, que previamente haya elegido el conductor.
text.en: It is responsible for not exceeding a speed, the limited speed, previously chosen by the driver.

explanation.text:
DRIVING ASSIST SYSTEMS
13 Intelligent Speed Assistant (ISA)
The system helps to ensure the driver is aware of and respects the speed limit, acting on the transmission system to adapt the vehicle’s speed to the limit on the road along which it is travelling.
(Página 92 del manual 'Learning to drive')
DRIVING ASSIST SYSTEMS
13 Intelligent Speed Assistant (ISA)
The system is linked to the TSR system, using a frontfacing camera and GPS in combination with a digital map to detect the speed limit for each stretch of road, informing the driver graphically through the instrument panel. It also automatically adapts the vehicle’s maximum speed to the limits in force on each stretch of the road, and does not allow the driver to accelerate beyond the speed allowed.
It can be activated and deactivated manually by clicking on a button or by pressing the accelerator.

13 Driver Distraction and Drowsiness Recognition (DDR)
The system assesses the driver’s level of attention in situations where he/she may lose concentration at the wheel, because of fatigue, sleepiness or other reasons.
The system monitors several aspects of the driver’s face, including how open his/her eyes are. It also analyses driving patterns and the driver’s reactions, combining them with driving speed data, the time and the use of indicators. If it detects that the driver is tired, it warns him/her by an acoustic or visual alert (displaying a coffee cup on the dashboard) or by making the steering wheel or seat vibrate, indicating the need for a break.

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
2.2 Factors involved in collisions
Generally, the factors that influence the occurrence of a traffic collision are varied, but always one or more of these factors are involved: the
vehicle, the road (& environment) and the driver.
Not all risk factors are equally important. Of every 100 collisions, only between
4 and 13 are due mainly to vehicle factors
(for example, a defective tyre or deficient brakes) and only
between 10 and 35 are due mainly to the road and related environment factors
(for example, when the roadway is wet and the vehicle loses control).
Most collisions,
between 70 and 90%, are due to the human factor
(for example, the driver becomes distracted, or speeds or is under the influence of alcohol etc).

explanation.text:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.3 Depression
It is the
most common
form of mental suffering. The principal
symptoms
are: a sad mood, anxious or empty feeling, listlessness, lack of energy and feelings of hopelessness and pessimism. If suffering from depression, it is best to get
specialist assistance
as soon as possible.
(Página 48 del manual 'Learning to drive')
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.3 Depression
Depression affects the capabilities of the driver:
Increasing distractions.
The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.
Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant.
The driver
fails to detect
significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.
Increasing insecurity.
Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.
Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue.
It is advisable not to drive at night or in environments where road monotony may occur or for long periods of time.
Increasing irritability and anxiety.
A trivial event can provoke a disproportionate reaction by the driver.
In addition, there is usually the need for
psychotropic drugs,
which can directly affect the ability to drive.

duration

ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.1 Respiratory allergies
Allergic rhinitis
can reduce the
psycho-physical fitness
to drive by up
to 42%

risk of a collision
.

symptoms

cold

reckless

when driving.

disregard

decisions
. It takes more time to think and reactions become
slower
with the potential for more
errors
.
A lower level of
concentration
whilst driving in traffic, which increases the likelihood of being
distracted
.
The speeding up and emergence of
fatigue
when driving.

poorly maintained road

FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES

quality of sleep

Aquaplaning
(also referred to occasionally as ‘hydroplaning’) is a frightening phenomenon whereby a wedge (or film) of water builds up between the tyres and the road surface. The
depth of water
on the road may be
excessive for the grooves
of the tyre
to suitably displace it
, which may also be heightened because of an inadequate depth of tyre tread.
This causes the vehicle to feel like it is “gliding or sliding on the water”. The result is complete
loss of normal control by the driver.
(Página 228 del manual 'Learning to drive')
Safe driving
5 Driving in rain
5.1.1 Aquaplaning
Aquaplaning is caused by the accumulation of water on the road and by irregularities in its surface. Therefore, when it rains, it is necessary to pay
special attention
to
potholes
and areas in which
puddles
may occur.
This effect is more likely to occur with inappropriate speed and very wide or badly worn tyres.
One of the best solutions to avoid aquaplaning is to
reduce the speed
in the first instance, so that the tyres can displace the water and the wheels can retain contact with the road surface.

The following explains the order of preference in the absence of road signs, signals or authorised persons, and applies to priority when different types of vehicles approach a narrow road section and it is necessary for one of the vehicles to reverse back to allow the other vehicle to pass. Under these circumstance priority is given as follows:
1.Special vehicles and those travelling under special regulations that exceed the established masses and dimensions as per the regulated rules of vehicles (MAM).

Road traffic collisions
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
2.2 Factors involved in collisions
Generally, the factors that influence the occurrence of a traffic collision are varied, but always one or more of these factors are involved: the
vehicle, the road (& environment) and the driver.
Not all risk factors are equally important. Of every 100 collisions, only between
4 and 13 are due mainly to vehicle factors
(for example, a defective tyre or deficient brakes) and only
between 10 and 35 are due mainly to the road and related environment factors
(for example, when the roadway is wet and the vehicle loses control).
Most collisions,
between 70 and 90%, are due to the human factor
(for example, the driver becomes distracted, or speeds or is under the influence of alcohol etc).

8.2 Advise: Request for help
Before requesting help you should make a
quick assessment of the scene.
The following information will be needed; the exact location, the road and locality; the number, type of vehicles involved; the number of casualties and degree of injury and so on.
If it is apparent that there is someone
severely injured or fatalities,
it is obligatory to advise the relevant authorities and you should
stay at the scene of the accident until they arrive.
You should only leave when the authorities say that it is permissible to do so or in order to aid the injured or to be attended to yourself.
It is also compulsory to notify the authorities if any of the parties involved in the accident so request, even when there are no injured parties and road safety was re-established.

(adjacent) to a twowheeled vehicle.
Maintain an
adequate and safe separation distance,

bad weather or poor visibility;

reduce the risk

minimise injury

It is also possible to avoid many of the risk factors that are connected with the vehicle, the road or the environment.

DISTRACTIONS

Studies show that traffic collisions are the

ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS

The amount of alcohol ingested.

higher strength

of a drink with a
lower strength
(such as beer).
(Página 41 del manual 'Learning to drive')
ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS

thicker set
.

woman

higher

ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS

Whether the stomach is empty or full.
The amount of alcohol in the blood is
higher
when drinking on an

amount
of food and the

of food, which are both factors in varying the speed at which the alcohol enters into the blood. However, this only slows the absorption, in the end the alcohol always reaches the blood.
Age. Children under 18

question.es: Entre los costes por daños materiales causados por los accidentes de tráfico se encuentran los daños producidos...

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

Any driver of a vehicle driving behind another must leave space that allows them to stop without colliding in the event of sudden braking, taking into account, in particular, speed, grip and braking conditions. However, a group of cyclists does not need to keep this distance, paying close attention to avoid collisions.
When it is possible for vehicles behind you to overtake, then in addition to leaving a sufficient separation distance so that in case of sudden braking by the vehicle ahead of you – you don’t crash into the back of it, you should additionally leave a gap to allow overtaking vehicles to overtake safely. (Note: that his rule is not applicable to a group of cyclists travelling together.)

explanation.text:
Road traffic collisions
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the
enormous economic impact
(either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs
derived from road traffic accidents are classified as
human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human
costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering.
Material
costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment.
Healthcare
costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations.
Administrative
costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

All drivers when passing or crossing other vehicles and users should always leave a sufficient (side) separation distance so as to avoid any likelihood of danger and potential impact. This is referred to as ‘lateral’ separation.

The weather and environmental conditions.

RISK GROUPS
5 Pedestrians
5.3.1 Forward Collision Warning with detection of Pedestrians and Cyclists (FCW+P+C)
This system monitors conditions on the road and in the surrounding area, warning the driver when it estimates a high probability of collision with other vehicles or with pedestrians or cyclists. It uses an acoustic or visual signal or vibration to alert the driver.

prevent

Lighting, tyres and brakes are
active safety systems
.
(Página 62 del manual 'Learning to drive')
1 Influence of the vehicle in traffic collisions

Passive safety or secondary safety,
aim to
minimise the damage

completely nullify

3 Brakes

When an automobile is
not under acceleration,
the engine helps
to hold back
the vehicle. This restraint is all the greater when a
lower ratio gear
is used. This is known as “engine braking.”

As a general rule, no more than eight points can be lost in a single day.
When drivers receive a
non-appealable
sanction in an administrative proceeding for committing any of the serious or very serious infractions that entail a loss of points, the points that are lost will be automatically and simultaneously
deducted
at the time when the violation is entered into the
Registry of Drivers and Offenders.
If one year has passed since the penalty became final and the related offence has not been recorded, the points will not be deducted.
A licence can be withdrawn as a consequence of losing
all
available points.
It is then not possible to obtain
a new licence for
six months
(three months for a professional driver).

FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
13 Driver Distraction and Drowsiness Recognition (DDR)
The system assesses the driver’s level of attention in situations where he/she may lose concentration at the wheel, because of fatigue, sleepiness or other reasons.
The system monitors several aspects of the driver’s face, including how open his/her eyes are. It also analyses driving patterns and the driver’s reactions, combining them with driving speed data, the time and the use of indicators. If it detects that the driver is tired, it warns him/her by an acoustic or visual alert (displaying a coffee cup on the dashboard) or by making the steering wheel or seat vibrate, indicating the need for a break.

explanation.text:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.3 Depression
It is the
most common
form of mental suffering. The principal
symptoms
are: a sad mood, anxious or empty feeling, listlessness, lack of energy and feelings of hopelessness and pessimism. If suffering from depression, it is best to get
specialist assistance
as soon as possible.
(Página 48 del manual 'Learning to drive')
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.3 Depression
Depression affects the capabilities of the driver:
Increasing distractions.
The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.
Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant.
The driver
fails to detect
significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.
Increasing insecurity.
Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.
Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue.
It is advisable not to drive at night or in environments where road monotony may occur or for long periods of time.
Increasing irritability and anxiety.
A trivial event can provoke a disproportionate reaction by the driver.
In addition, there is usually the need for
psychotropic drugs,
which can directly affect the ability to drive.

22 General Precautions
Not everyone responds well or the same to medication.
The age, the habit of use, physical condition of the user or other circumstances may
vary the effects
of the drugs.

Always consult the doctor or pharmacist.
Use medications properly.
Never self-medicate.

explanation.text:
OTHER FACTORS
25 Clothing
25.1 The clothing of motorcyclist
A motorcycle does not provide the rider with a secure and protective shell. This makes the rider vulnerable in road traffic collisions; to the elements, such as, in the cold, wind, rain, and so on. The body of the rider and any passenger realises the force of all of these external elements, the weather and any possible impact. It is therefore absolutely essential to use a
dress code that adequately protects
them
all of the time regardless of the time of year.
The motorcyclist’s outfit has to be
colourful and eye-catching,
and should be made of
leather or other similar material
. It should have contrasting colours and design, with reflective bands that allow it to be distinguished from a distance.
A ‘set of leathers’ (a leather jacket and trousers) is advocated, as it will:
Does not flap with the air.
Protects against the wind during the trip.
Provide protection from possible damage, scrapes and consequent rubbing or contact sores to the rider. In the event of falling off abrasive wounds are minimised.

25 Clothing

When riding a motorcycle it is recommendable to wear
gloves
. If the rider falls or slips off typically the hands receive the force and impact as the rider automatically responds with the hands. Inevitably
grazes and wounds
, subject to the risk also of
serious infection
, will occur to the hands without gloves. The most suitable type are
leather gloves
that should not be too restrictive and allow for a
firm grip
to be maintained. They should be
lined
and have protective areas, with
ventilation
whilst also being
light in weight
.
Strong, protective boots
are another must for the rider. These protect the feet and
ankles
(it is advisable that they are higher in length, to also protect the legs). Ideally they should be
leather,
with
small heels,
so as to hold well in the stirrups or rests.
Always avoid
using sandals, sports shoes or other unsuitable footwear that offer only minimal protection.

Today many vehicles incorporate safety features as a standard matter of course. These provide the driver, occupants and other road users with a high level of safety and security when travelling. However, statistics show that new vehicles with greater technological advances, suffer proportionately
more accidents
than older vehicles, when it would have been logical for the reverse to apply; namely, older vehicles to suffer more collisions.
One of the reasons might be that very few drivers know
how the new technology works and what the systems provide
for their vehicles so that such features, rather than being advantageous, become an inconvenience and sometimes a danger.
(Página 61 del manual 'Learning to drive')
1 Influence of the vehicle in traffic collisions
1.2 Vehicle safety features
Whilst, on the other hand, there are many drivers who, knowing that their vehicles have these latest developments installed, feel
more secure
and, consciously or unconsciously,
take more risks
, unaware and oblivious to the fact that any security system always operates
within certain limits
.
For a safety system to be effective the driver must know how to operate it and how it works and, above all,
how to drive
accordingly. It is therefore very important to read carefully the technical manual of the car and learn how to
properly use
the safety systems installed.

ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES
4 Wheels

4.2.3 The tread pattern
The tread pattern is the set of grooves in the tread of a tire. In addition to
gripping the road surface,
it must guarantee good drainage away of the surface water from the tyre. The adhesion between the tyre and the road is reduced when the tyre is worn.
All tyres, (including retreads) must always
comply with the legal requirements.
This includes, not only the tyre tread and depth of pattern but also other abnormalities relating to the tyre-wall and tread, inflation pressure, bulges, exposed cords, cuts and other signs of irregular wear, and also the mixing of tyres etc. Basically the carcass (housing) must comply with all legal requirements.
The tyres of the vehicles within categories
M1, N1, O1 and O2
(See Unit 1, article 14) must, when used on the public roads (or places recognised as public thorough fares), have a
minimum depth of tread, of 1.6 mm,
in a continuous band in the main grooves of the contact surface.
Note: There are other requirements relating to the depth of tread and pattern.

Stay calm.

However, this does not guarantee that in a collision the occupants will not suffer injury. Firstly, occupant safety measures

explanation.text:
7 Seat belts
7.1 Purpose and effectiveness
The purpose of a seat belt is to
retain and protect
the
driver and occupants
in the event of sudden stopping, collision or the vehicle rolling over. The seat belt
prevents
the occupants of a vehicle from being
catapulted out
of it and
absorbs
part of the energy of an impact.
During a frontal collision against an indeformable object, a vehicle stops in a tenth of a second, but due to inertia, the occupants will continue moving
at the same speed
as the
vehicle
was travelling at. Therefore, there is the likelihood of colliding with the steering wheel or the windshield, which will result in
serious injuries
being sustained.
To avoid this, the seat belt slows the movement of the body by
stretching out
, as if is made of an elastic material, by an extensible action.
(Página 75 del manual 'Learning to drive')
7 Seat belts
7.6 Misconceptions of safety belts
"In town, a seat belt is not necessary, as the speed is low”
At only 30 or 40 kilometres per hour an accident can be fatal if the head hits the sun visor, dash board or steering wheel.
In an impact at low-speed, the safety belt will normally ensure that the occupants escape unhurt or suffer minor injury.
"In short journeys seat belts aren’tneeded”
Most accidents involving casualties occur within a few kilometres from the place of departure, so it’s important to use seat belts on all journeys.

7 Seat belts
7.6 Misconceptions of safety belts
“It is dangerous to use a seat belt during pregnancy”
The use of seat belts is compulsory for pregnant women, as they have proved that if you are not wearing it, the foetus can suffer major damage in the event of an accident.
The abdominal belt must go as low as possible on the hips, to wear it higher could potentially harm the baby. There are devices on the market that adequately prevent the belt from going up onto the abdomen.
“The belt is only necessary for front seat passengers. In the rear seats it isn’ necessary”
If passengers in the rear seats fail to wear a seat belt there is the probability that, in the event of a frontal collision, they will be fired forwards towards the occupants in the front seats and serious injury will be caused.
The likelihood for an occupant in the rear seats to cause the death of another passenger in the front seats due to the fact that they are launched forward is up to 8 times greater than if the seat belt is worn.

explanation.text:
11 Motorcycle - seating
A proper body position on the motorcycle is more comfortable and leads to safer driving. The rider will be able to react more quickly to any eventuality that may arise.
The golden rule is that the body should be in a
natural position, relaxed and not tense.
The body should be slightly crouched, just enough to reach the handlebars, with the
arms and hands relaxed
to reduce fatigue.
Unnatural positions,
such as being in an over or under crouching position will result in the elbows being up too high or having over stretched arms, this will lead to an
increase of fatigue
and reduce control of the vehicle.

18 Hill Holder assistance system

DRIVING ASSIST SYSTEMS
20 Rear Cross Traffic Alert (RCTA)
The system monitors traffic crossing behind the vehicle when it reverses out of a parallel parking space. Vehicles approaching on either side can be detected with radar or ultrasonic sensors. If the system detects a vehicle approaching and there is a risk of collision, a sound is emitted or a visual warning is shown.
Some manufacturers have incorporated a system that fully applies the brakes automatically in the event of an imminent collision, if the driver does not react to the warning, provided that the vehicle is travelling at less than 15 km/h.

5 Generic speed
5.1 Maximum speed limits on interurban roads

Special vehicles and sets of special vehicles:
If they lack brake lights, or tow a trailer or are cultivators –a maximum speed of
25 km/h.
If they are capable of reaching a speed of 60 km/h on flat ground, and comply with the signalling regulations of vehicles: - a maximum speed of

In all other cases, the maximum speed for the remaining special vehicles is
40 km/h.
Note:
All these vehicles are
legally obligated
to show, to the rear of the vehicle, the sign
V-4
(limited speed sign). This must be displayed so that it is clearly visible.

8 Speed limits are a necessity
Speed limits are not capricious. There are numerous
factors
that determine the implementation of a certain speed limit being imposed, (for example; the designated speed, the acceptable degree of congestion, the demands of existing traffic, etc.) The aim of a set speed limit is to allow vehicles to travel with the maximum
guarantee of safety and fluidity.
One of the most important criteria is the
designated speed
of the road (the maximum safe speed that can be maintained on a section of road under favourable conditions). This means that a road is designated to be used at a certain generic or specific speed limit and traffic is not allowed to do a higher speed than that specified. To do
otherwise means that safety will be compromised.

explanation.text:
12 Distances
12.1 The reaction distance
The
reaction distance
is the distance travelled by the vehicle from the time of seeing a hazard until he reacts to it.
It is dependant on the
speed
and the driver’s
reaction time,
which in turn depends, on many other factors, such as, the driver’s reflexes, their psycho-physical state (level of alertness, whether or not the driver is under the influence of alcohol etc.) Even the environment can affect the time it takes for a driver to react to any given circumstance (the passenger compartment temperature, noise, etc.)
A reaction time of
0.75 seconds
is considered to be
normal,
during which time the vehicle will travel a distance, determined by the
speed
at which the vehicle is travelling.

text.en: Yes, it decreases it.

text.es: No.
text.en: No.

text.es: Sí, lo aumenta.
text.en: Yes, it increases it.

explanation.text:
Physical condition of the driver
4 Reaction time
The reaction time can be increased by:
fatigue or tiredness,
drowsiness, sleepiness,
the advancement of age,
the loss of vision and poor hearing,
poor state of health,
the use of medications,
the intake of alcohol, drugs or other narcotics substances,
heavy and excessive meals,
the excessive heat in the cockpit of the vehicle,
the emotional state.
the attention level of the driver.
All these listed factors have the serious potential consequence of reducing the driver’s ability to react and therefore the result is an increase in the reaction time.
(Página 32 del manual 'Learning to drive')
12 Distances
12.1 The reaction distance
The
reaction distance
is the distance travelled by the vehicle from the time of seeing a hazard until he reacts to it.
It is dependant on the
speed
and the driver’s
reaction time,
which in turn depends, on many other factors, such as, the driver’s reflexes, their psycho-physical state (level of alertness, whether or not the driver is under the influence of alcohol etc.) Even the environment can affect the time it takes for a driver to react to any given circumstance (the passenger compartment temperature, noise, etc.)
A reaction time of
0.75 seconds
is considered to be
normal,
during which time the vehicle will travel a distance, determined by the
speed
at which the vehicle is travelling.

12.2 The braking distance
The braking distance is the
distance the vehicle travels
from the point at which the driver first
applies the brakes,
until the vehicle come to a
complete stop.
This distance can vary depending on:
The
speed
of the vehicle at the point the brakes are applied.
The
mass
of the
vehicle
and its
load.
The
technical condition
of the vehicle (brakes, tyres, shock absorbers, etc.)
The
environmental conditions
and the condition of the
road surface
(snow, rain, state of the surface, etc.)
The
driver
(psychophysical status –mental and physical state, experience, etc.)
An
increase
in
speed
causes the braking distance to increase, but this is at a greater rate than the speed increase.
Thus, when the velocity is doubled the braking distance is four times higher.

The
overall stopping distance
is the
